##### List of Business Rules discussed on July 14 
###### **Exhaustive List of Business Rules**
**1. Branding & Identity**
  - **Logo Tagline Integration:** The Keydemand logo used in the UI must include the "CRE simplified" tagline, as this is part of the officially registered logo and standard marketing language used across all creatives.
**2. User Accounts & Tracking**
  - **No User Impersonation ("Switch" Feature):** A Keydemand admin or assigned demand team user cannot use a brand’s profile/account on their behalf to contact properties. All actions logged under "properties contacted" must strictly be the brand user's own actions.
**3. Dashboard UI & Terminology**
  - **Card Constraints:** The dashboard UI must strictly maintain six total cards to ensure a clean UI/UX.
  - **Leads Terminology:** The term "Leads received" is being deprecated in favor of simply "Leads".
  - **Consolidated Leads Card:** Because of the six-card limit, the main Leads card (the green card) must encompass both "inbound" metrics (e.g., leads received, image requests) and "outbound" metrics (outbound contacts). Outbound contacts will likely be added as a floating element within this single card.
  - **Contextual "User Types":** The platform defines "User Type" in two distinct contexts that must not be confused:
      - *Population Level:* Defined at Keydemand’s end (e.g., broker, brand user).
      - *Project/Inquiry Level:* Defined as roles like Tenant, Agent, or Developer.
**4. Property Display & Interaction UX**
  - **Hidden Property Display:** For properties that a user uploads but marks as "hidden," the UI must not rely solely on an eye icon. Because the photo area is small, an opacity change (or similar visual treatment) must be used so the user can still read the property details.
  - **Internal Visibility of Hidden Properties:** If a property is marked hidden by a specific user (e.g., Himanshu), it must remain fully accessible and viewable to authorized internal users/managers (e.g., Kartik), clearly indicating who hid it.
  - **Clickable Property Cards:** Clicking anywhere on the general background of a property card must open that specific property's page.
  - **Hover States:** When a user hovers over a fully clickable card, the background must light up/highlight (e.g., in a green or blue shade) to clearly indicate it is clickable.
  - **Exclusion from General Clickability:** The four specific call-to-action buttons on a card (Relevancy, Edit, Detail, etc.) act independently and are excluded from the general card hover/click rules.
  - **Information-Dense Cards:** Cards containing heavy amounts of information should utilize a subtle shadow rather than color-changing backgrounds on hover to avoid overwhelming the user.
##### List of business rules on July 16
**1. Enterprise Dashboard & High-Value Leads UI Logic**
  - **Actionable Buttons Restriction:** Enterprise brands (acting as Keydemand team users) do not have "Accept," "Reject," or "Image Request" buttons for leads. "Leads Open" solely functions to open and view the lead.
  - **High-Value KD Tickets Display:** For high-value leads where a demand is matched, the UI must explicitly display the demand card, its specific relevancy score, and the property/project owner's details.
  - **"My Task" Shortcut Functionality:** The "My Task" section acts as a shortcut view displaying items marked with a red indicator, specifically representing unviewed or unopened property leads and demand leads.
  - **Enterprise 'All Accounts' Card Data:** The Enterprise assigned accounts table must display "Relevancy" data. Relevancy details must encompass the Demand ID, a clickable Relevant Property ID (which opens the property page), relevancy percentage, place, and size.
  - **Mobile UI Abbreviations:** To prevent text wrapping issues on mobile screens, internal team dashboards can utilize abbreviations (e.g., "KD" instead of "Keydemand Properties") subject to final UX review.
**2. Property Posting & Form Logic**
  - **Other Interested Locations Field:** The "Other Interested Location" field must be supported across Retail, FNB, Office, and Managed Spaces. It must accommodate up to three multiple secondary locations alongside the primary location. Same city, no radius
  - In the filters field in all properties page, we need to have an option to select range between example 1000 to 2000. the range is to short to select the option 1000 to 2000
##### July 29th - Business rules and Action items 
<https://docs.google.com/document/d/14nXV4QvzlIE3JwqOsDNOIOhJC4UmCBHO6hqFAE_24SI/edit?tab=t.0>
###### **Business Rules**
**Demand Images & Brand Logos**
  - Uploaded enterprise brand logos must display as the small avatar (icon) on demand cards.
  - If the end-user provides no brand logo, system-defined placeholder images based on the specific asset class (e.g., office, retail) must be used.
  - On the detailed demand page, no large images or photos should be shown, as demands represent requirements and lack tangible media.
  - If a brand (e.g., Starbucks) registers independently and does not upload a photo, the system should simply display their initial and name (e.g., "posted by Starbucks") rather than a large empty thumbnail.
  - A feature to mask or hide brand names/logos for enterprise clients who request anonymity (e.g., Levi's) is noted as a business necessity but has been parked for future phases.
**Demand & Property Display Logic**
  - Demand cards must be structurally lean (approximately 15 fields) compared to property cards (25-30 fields) because they do not require heavy media attachments or floor plans.
  - "Explore Demands" and "Explore Properties" cannot coexist in a single scrolling feed or multi-select search because their filter logic and fields are polar opposites and would confuse users.
  - Only "Keydemand" users possess the system permissions to explore demands; regular users, brands, and agents do not have this option.
  - "Properties" and "Projects" both represent supply inventory and can be multi-selected and viewed together.
  - Selecting "Demands" in the search parameters must automatically deselect "Properties" and "Projects".
**Platform Navigation & Global Filters**
  - The primary navbar menu item on Keydemand navbar must be renamed from "Explore Properties" to a consolidated "Explore Listings".
  - Under "Explore Listings," users will use radio buttons to explicitly toggle between exploring demands or properties.
  - When searching for Projects, the following filters must be present: Transaction type, Project size, Possession date, Project type, City, Location, and Asset class.
  - "Asset Class" and "Project Type" are mandatory filter fields for Projects.
**User Onboarding, Consent & Landing Pages**
  - The "18 and above" age consent checkbox and the Terms of Use link on the login modal have been verified as fully implemented and correct.
  - For unregistered users, a new "List a Project" button must be present on the global navbar to act as a primary acquisition hook for Developers and Managed Space Operators.
  - Developer and Managed Space Operator registration entry points must be removed from the standard login popup. They are to be moved into the "List a Project" flow, forcing users to explicitly select their user type via radio button to reveal the registration form.
  - The landing page client section must feature static, non-clickable category text reading: Retail & F&B Brands, Developers, Mall Operators, Office Tenants, and Managed Space Operators.
  - The "Explore Clients" UI must specifically utilize the verified list of client logos located in Columns G and H of the PR sheet (e.g., Postman, which has 5 offices in Bangalore).
  - The "8,000+ properties" banner on the landing page will feature complete client lists, while the banner on the About Us page will feature select bits of client information.
**User Roles & Relationship Managers (RMs)**
  - Brokers are not assigned Relationship Managers (BRMs do not exist in the system).
  - Enterprise and Brand users (e.g., retail and F&B brands) are assigned RMs.
  - If multiple Key Demand team members are assigned to manage a single brand's account, only the **first** person assigned will be publicly displayed as the designated RM on the brand's dashboard.

### July 29th - Business rules and Action items  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** Google Doc · ID `14nXV4QvzlIE3JwqOsDNOIOhJC4UmCBHO6hqFAE_24SI` · owner pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · created 2026-07-29, modified 2026-08-03 · sections read: Business Rules (5 sub-sections), Key Action Items & Tasks table · no comments · read coverage: 100%.

#### Content
##### Business Rules
**Demand Images & Brand Logos**
- Uploaded enterprise brand logos must display as the small avatar (icon) on demand cards.
- If the end-user provides no brand logo, system-defined placeholder images based on the specific asset class (e.g., office, retail) must be used.
- On the detailed demand page, no large images or photos should be shown, as demands represent requirements and lack tangible media.
- If a brand (e.g., Starbucks) registers independently and does not upload a photo, the system should simply display their initial and name (e.g., "posted by Starbucks") rather than a large empty thumbnail.
- A feature to mask or hide brand names/logos for enterprise clients who request anonymity (e.g., Levi's) is noted as a business necessity but has been parked for future phases.

**Demand & Property Display Logic**
- Demand cards must be structurally lean (approximately 15 fields) compared to property cards (25-30 fields) because they do not require heavy media attachments or floor plans.
- "Explore Demands" and "Explore Properties" cannot coexist in a single scrolling feed or multi-select search because their filter logic and fields are polar opposites and would confuse users.
- Only "Keydemand" users possess the system permissions to explore demands; regular users, brands, and agents do not have this option.
- "Properties" and "Projects" both represent supply inventory and can be multi-selected and viewed together.
- Selecting "Demands" in the search parameters must automatically deselect "Properties" and "Projects".

**Platform Navigation & Global Filters**
- The primary navbar menu item on Keydemand navbar must be renamed from "Explore Properties" to a consolidated "Explore Listings".
- Under "Explore Listings," users will use radio buttons to explicitly toggle between exploring demands or properties.
- When searching for Projects, the following filters must be present: Transaction type, Project size, Possession date, Project type, City, Location, and Asset class.
- "Asset Class" and "Project Type" are mandatory filter fields for Projects.

**User Onboarding, Consent & Landing Pages**
- The "18 and above" age consent checkbox and the Terms of Use link on the login modal have been verified as fully implemented and correct.
- For unregistered users, a new "List a Project" button must be present on the global navbar to act as a primary acquisition hook for Developers and Managed Space Operators.
- Developer and Managed Space Operator registration entry points must be removed from the standard login popup. They are to be moved into the "List a Project" flow, forcing users to explicitly select their user type via radio button to reveal the registration form.
- The landing page client section must feature static, non-clickable category text reading: Retail & F&B Brands, Developers, Mall Operators, Office Tenants, and Managed Space Operators.
- The "Explore Clients" UI must specifically utilize the verified list of client logos located in Columns G and H of the PR sheet (e.g., Postman, which has 5 offices in Bangalore).
- The "8,000+ properties" banner on the landing page will feature complete client lists, while the banner on the About Us page will feature select bits of client information.

**User Roles & Relationship Managers (RMs)**
- Brokers are not assigned Relationship Managers (BRMs do not exist in the system).
- Enterprise and Brand users (e.g., retail and F&B brands) are assigned RMs.
- If multiple Key Demand team members are assigned to manage a single brand's account, only the **first** person assigned will be publicly displayed as the designated RM on the brand's dashboard.

##### Client Discussions June 4th Week
**UI, UX, and Content Changes**
- **Property Detail Access:** Implement functionality allowing unregistered users to view property details by default.
- **Image Masking:** Ensure property images are masked/blacked out for unregistered users *only* if the broker specifically opted to hide them.
- **CTA Restrictions:** Ensure unregistered users are prompted to register only when clicking actionable elements like "View Phone Number" or "Contact Us".
- **Incentive Messaging:** Design and implement a pre-wall popup or graphic communicating the "one free listing" reward to users *before* they begin the registration flow, rather than showing it post-registration.
- **Dashboard Subscription Text:** Remove placeholder text on the agent dashboard/profile pages and replace it with accurate status labels (e.g., "Free Plan," "Trial Plan," "Usage 0 of 1") and a "Subscribe Now for unlimited access" call to action.
- **Navbar Inquiry Button:** Add a "List your project" (Developer/Managed Space Inquiry) button to the top navigation bar that triggers an inquiry form without requiring a user login.
- **Landing Page City Tabs:** Remove static city tabs from the exclusive projects section. Make the city tabs for sponsored projects dynamic so they only display cities with active project inventory.
- **Default Search Bug:** Fix the bug where the default city selection is not automatically defaulting to Bangalore.
- **Google Maps Integration:** Integrate Google Maps into the search/typing functionality for accurate locality selection (to be evaluated for performance impact).
- **Dashboard Cleanup:** Remove the redundant "lead management" section from the agent dashboard to prevent duplication and realign the fourth tab on the dashboard.
- **Client Logos:** Add the names and logos for "Office Tenant" and "Managed Office Spaces" to the static client section on the landing page.
- **Form Validations:** Add a vibrating notification or explicit visual indicator to alert users when mandatory fields are missed during form submission.
- **Text Updates:** Revise website content/write-ups for clarity. Standardize user terminology across the platform by changing "Agent" to "Property Agent" and "Tenant" to "Office Tenant".
- **PDF Functionality:** Implement the missing PDF download feature for individual user listings.
- **SEO Compliance:** Populate the necessary website data and tags to ensure the platform is fully SEO compliant.

**Forms, Registration & Lead Capture**
- **Immediate Lead Capture:** Update the "Show Interest" API logic to capture the phone number as a lead the exact moment OTP verification is successful, preventing lead loss if the user closes the browser before finishing.
- **Standardize Mandatory Fields:** Update the quick registration journey to mirror the exact mandatory fields required when posting a demand (e.g., floor preference, carpet area, transaction type) to ensure backend relevancy matching does not break later.
- **Form Cleanup:** Remove the email address field from the user registration form completely, as it causes validation failures in the "Show Interest" flow.
- **Field Editability:** Change system logic to allow users to edit 'Yes' fields in property and demand forms even after a response is received.

**Business Rules & Platform Logic Evaluations**
- **High-Value Demand Routing:** Develop a simplified, hardcoded logic model to route high-end requirements (e.g., above 5,000 sq ft) exclusively to Key Demand team members based on specific cities (Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore, Chennai, Indore, Hyderabad).
- **Demand Volume Restrictions:** Confirm with the business team whether city-specific demand volume restrictions (e.g., hiding 10,000+ sq ft demands from public view) will be implemented in Phase 1 or deferred to Phase 2.
- **Cross-Asset Exploration:** Finalize the logic allowing Retail and Food & Beverage (FNB) brands to explore each other's properties to maximize leads, while restricting their ability to post demands to their registered asset class.
- **Tenant Logic Verification:** Confirm the rule that Office tenants can post and explore both Office and Managed Spaces, while Managed Space tenants can explore Office but only post Managed Space.
- **Lead Visibility:** Decide whether Key Demand agents should have a centralized Pan-India view of high-end leads or if visibility should be strictly restricted to their assigned cities.
- **Metric Redundancy:** Evaluate if the "Leads Received" and "Contact Inquiries" counters are doing the exact same thing and determine if one should be removed to avoid confusion.
- Enterprise brands cannot manage sub-users themselves; these must be managed via the Key Demand backend admin panel.
- **Update Client Logos:** Provide names and logos for the new "office tenant" and "managed office space" users to be added to the client logos section.

**Compliance, Legal, & Admin**
- **Mandatory Checkboxes:** Add a mandatory Terms and Conditions / Privacy Policy checkbox to *all* registration flows (a simple "Proceed" button was deemed legally insufficient).
- **Phone Number Consent:** Add explicit terms regarding phone number disclosure to the registration process so users know their number is shared upon a request.
- **Legal Documentation:** Review the pending Terms of Use and Privacy Policy documentation (expected by the 10th) to ensure it satisfies both European GDPR and Indian DPDP Acts.
- **Data Deletion:** Implement a mechanism for automated "right to erase" or account deletion requests to comply with data laws.
- **Compliance Fields:** Add mandatory fields for Project RERA registration numbers and appoint a dedicated platform Grievance Officer. Determine if agent registration numbers are legally necessary for commercial properties.
- **Admin Panel Roles:** Finalize the precise user permissions for Admin groups (A, B, and C) and populate the administrative input fields.

Keydemand team: They can view my listings and all Keydemand listings under the dashboard, with a separate section to showcase as My listing / Keydemand listing

### Recent enhancements  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** Google Doc · ID `1ayBF6ywdSTdCRePAJD7dchfFGOMFSbj9l3FcWAHREso` · owner pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · created/modified 2026-06-30 · sections read: intro + sections 1–7 · no comments · read coverage: 100%.

#### Content
This comprehensive summary consolidates all technical requirements, business logic for the development of Keydemand V2.

##### 1. Standardized Nomenclature & User Roles
To eliminate ambiguity between the frontend and backend, the following terminology is finalized:
- **Agent:** (Formerly "Agent")
- **Office Tenant:** (Formerly "Tenant")
- **Account Handler:** The standardized term for the internal Keydemand team/backend.
- **Relationship Manager (RM):** The external-facing title for the internal staff member assigned to a brand/enterprise.
- **Developers/Mall Operators:** Specialized users for large-scale projects and mall listings.

##### 2. Exploration Logic & "Asset Lock" Rules
The platform balances open discovery with strict posting integrity through a dual-mode logic:
- **Unregistered User Access:** Property detail pages are now public including property images to unregistered users to improve SEO and user acquisition. However, a registration/login wall is triggered for specific actions: Viewing phone numbers, requesting locked images, or clicking "Contact Us."
- **Cross-Asset Exploration:** Registered users (Retail, FNB, and Office) are authorized to explore property listings across *all* asset classes (excluding Managed Spaces) to maximize lead capture potential.
- **Posting Restrictions:** Posting capabilities remain strictly locked to the user's registered asset class to ensure data quality.
    - **Office Tenants:** Authorized to post for both "Office" and "Managed Space."
    - **Managed Space Tenants:** Restricted to posting *only* "Managed Space."
- **Enterprise Brands:** Can be provisioned with multiple asset classes (e.g., both FNB and Retail) at the backend, allowing them to post demands for any assigned category.

##### 3. Lead Generation & ShowIntrest Mechanics
The registration flow is optimized to reduce friction and prevent lead loss:
- **OTP-First Capture:** A lead (Mobile Number) must be captured and sent to the backend immediately upon successful **OTP verification**. The system must not wait for the user to complete the full profile. If the user drops off after OTP, it is flagged as an "Incomplete Lead."
- **Form Optimization:**
    - **Select Role** must be the first field.
    - **Email address** is moved to an optional/non-mandatory field.
- **Compliance:** An explicit, mandatory checkbox for "Terms of Use" and "Privacy Policy" must be present in all registration flows (compliance with DPDP/GDPR).
- **Incentive Messaging:** The "One Free Listing" reward must be prominently displayed **before** registration (Pre-Wall) to encourage sign-ups.

##### 4. High-Ticket Lead (HTL) Ecosystem
HTL logic is the primary revenue protection mechanic for Tier 1 markets:
- **Threshold Definition:** Requirements exceeding specific size thresholds (e.g., >10,000 SFT in Bangalore/Hyderabad; >5,000 SFT in Mumbai) are classified as HTLs. These thresholds must be editable by the Admin on a per-city basis.
- **Tier 1 Markets:** Focus includes Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, and Delhi. Leads in Tier 2 cities (e.g., Jaipur, Indore) remain open to all agents regardless of size.
- **The "Manual Unlock" Valve:** HTLs are initially diverted to an internal Keydemand roster. If the internal team cannot service the lead within a set timeframe (e.g., 3-4 days), the Admin can manually "unlock" it, making it visible to general **Property Agents** under "Relevancy."
- **Agent-Added Demands:** Requirements posted by agents themselves bypass HTL restrictions and are visible to other agents through the relevancy matching engine.

##### 5. Dashboard & Internal Portal Architecture
To support internal sales and BD staff (who may not be tech-savvy), the portal uses a highly explicit, partitioned menu:
- **Hamburger Menu Segments:** Every category is divided into **"My"** (User-specific) and **"Overall"** (Company-wide) views:
    1. **Listings:** My Listing vs. Keydemand Listing.
    2. **Projects:** My Projects (assigned) vs. All Projects.
    3. **Enterprise Accounts:** My Assigned vs. All Enterprise Accounts.
    4. **High Ticket Leads:** My Leads (city-specific) vs. Overall Leads.
- **Broker Management:** A dedicated view for team members to monitor broker onboarding progress and inventory added by external brokers in their region.
- **Grid Toggles:** Dashboards must feature a switch to toggle between "High-Value" and "Standard" inventory views.

##### 6. UI/UX & technical Enhancements
- **Image Privacy (Bokeh Effect):** Property images are hidden/masked if those been locked by the Agent. Masked images should use a blurred layer with a "Request for Images" CTA.
- **Image Shuffling:** For demands without brand logos, the UI should shuffle between a pool of five high-quality asset-class images to maintain a dynamic look.
- **Brand Fallback:** Cards should prioritize the **Brand Logo**. If unavailable, display the **Brand Name** and the **First Initial** as an icon.
- **Google Maps Integration:** Location search must integrate with Google Maps to allow for precise, locality-based filtering (similar to 99acres).
- **Field Editability:** Few fields can still remain editable even after a response/lead has been received to allow users to refine their data. Further details are there in PR sheet.

##### 7. Administrative & Control Panel Logic
- **Strict Access Separation:** The **Admin Control Panel** is restricted to a core team (Kartik, Sudanchu, Himmanu, Nitesh) for platform management (creating UserTypes, setting HTL caps, managing permissions).
- **Portal-Only Operations:** 100% of day-to-day business operations (Sales, BD, Broker Management) must happen within the **User Portal**, not the backend Admin panel.
- **Subscription UI:** Trial plan placeholders must be replaced with dynamic status text: *"You are on a Trial Plan. X of 1 Listings used. Subscribe for unlimited access."*

#### Business rules extracted
(Rules restated in the Final sheet/CR Doc — HTL tiers/unlock/agent exemption, T&C checkbox, pre-wall, image shuffling, grid toggles, portal-only operations — are not renumbered.)
- **BR-CR-362** — Terminology (30 Jun): "Account Handler" = internal team/backend term; "Relationship Manager (RM)" = external-facing title for staff assigned to a brand/enterprise; "Office Tenant" formerly "Tenant"; Developers/Mall Operators = large-scale projects and mall listings. _(§1)_
- **BR-CR-363** — Property detail pages public including images for unregistered users; login wall only for viewing phone numbers, requesting locked images, or "Contact Us". _(§2)_
- **BR-CR-364** — Retail, FNB and Office users explore all asset classes excluding Managed Spaces. _(§2 — superseded)_
- **BR-CR-365** — Enterprise brands can be provisioned with multiple asset classes (e.g., FNB and Retail) at backend and post demands for any assigned category. _(§2)_
- **BR-CR-366** — Drop-off after OTP is flagged as "Incomplete Lead". _(§3)_
- **BR-CR-367** — Registration form: "Select Role" is the first field; email optional/non-mandatory. _(§3)_
- **BR-CR-368** — HTL is the primary revenue-protection mechanic for Tier 1 markets; thresholds editable per city by Admin. _(§4)_
- **BR-CR-369** — Hamburger "My"/"Overall": Listings (My Listing vs Keydemand Listing), Projects (My Projects assigned vs All Projects), Enterprise Accounts (My Assigned vs All), High Ticket Leads (My Leads city-specific vs Overall). _(§5)_
- **BR-CR-370** — Broker Management view: monitor broker onboarding progress and inventory added by external brokers in the member's region. _(§5)_
- **BR-CR-371** — Locked images shown with blurred (Bokeh) layer and a "Request for Images" CTA. _(§6)_
- **BR-CR-372** — Brand fallback: Brand Logo first; else Brand Name and First Initial icon. _(§6)_
- **BR-CR-373** — Google Maps locality filtering similar to 99acres. _(§6)_
- **BR-CR-374** — Admin Control Panel core team (Kartik, Sudanchu, Himmanu, Nitesh) creates UserTypes, sets HTL caps, manages permissions. _(§7)_
- **BR-CR-375** — Trial status text exactly: "You are on a Trial Plan. X of 1 Listings used. Subscribe for unlimited access." _(§7)_

**4. Requirements more than 5K** - These are the high-value leads that will come to Keydemand team. (For all asset class except Managed offices)

Admin team will have the option to select a city (Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai & Indore) and then keep a minimum size for each city; after that, all the demands will be transferred to the users based on the threshold set.

Demands more than that minimum size will not be shown to the end audience but will only hit Keydemand from that specific city; these demands will not be showcased under the relevancy of any other users except the Keydemand team.

The demand can still match the relevant properties that are within the size that the user has posted, and they can connect. Eg We put a limit of 5000 in Mumbai, and the demand posted by a brand is 6000 sft. The high-value lead is sent to the Keydemand team in Mumbai. No agent will be able to see the relevant demand under their relevancy. ### Agent User Dashboard - Gaps and Clarifications  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** Google Doc · ID `1ZHkBPdxI-iN-k8wf0ZbR4caJUxuBmlC3U5qK7XaMPe0` · owner pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · created 2026-05-26, modified 2026-05-28 · sections read: Add/Edit/Delete/Deactivate Profile, Search and Filters, Property Management, Demand Management, Project Management, Notifications, 1 comment thread · read coverage: 100%

#### Content
##### Add/Edit/Delete/Deactivate Profile
1. Need business rules for Reactivation and Deletion for Profile? What is the flow
   - *Comment (John Abraham, RESOLVED):* "Can a request to reactivate be sent from the customers end?" (reply by Pradeepa PV, empty)
2. Once deactivated, or failed to subscribe then what happens? What happens when he logins in and can be reactivate it? What is the scope of the user who was subscribed before but is not? If a deactivated agent can function exactly like a regular 'registered but not subscribed' user, what is the business justification for applying the 'deactivated' status? What is the precise workflow to reactivate an account that has been deactivated due to prolonged non-renewal?

   Subscription Lifecycle: Where does the subscription renewal process fit into the overall lifecycle of a user who moves from 'subscribed' to 'expired' and finally to the 'deactivated' state? Do give us clarity on how it effects subscription?

**Answer — Subscription life cycle: Your subscription, explained**

**How billing works** — Your subscription is billed monthly and auto-charged on the same date each month. You don't need to do anything — it renews automatically.

**If you cancel** — You can cancel anytime from your account settings. Auto-renewal stops immediately, but you'll continue to enjoy full premium access until the end of your current billing cycle.

**If a payment fails** — If your auto-payment doesn't go through, we will give a button of renew on the users subscription page, where they can renew it.

**What happens to your listings after cancellation** — After your last successful payment, all your listings stay active on the platform for 3 months. This gives you time to view all your leads and relevancy but cannot connect with new users, the user has to resubscribe for not losing visibility. After those 3 months, all your listings will be deactivated. To bring them back live, simply resubscribe — your data stays safe with us in the meantime. The user needs to manually select all the listings to make it active.

**Deactivating your account pauses everything.** All your listings will be hidden, and you won't appear active on the platform. You can reactivate anytime — a "Reactivate account" button will be available on your home page when you return. Once reactivated, your account will be marked as registered but not subscribed.

**Note:** If you deactivate during an active subscription, your subscription benefits will resume automatically — as long as you reactivate within your original subscription period. If they re-activate outside the subscription flow then they will be a general registered user and has to go through the subscription process again or asked for subscription if they do any CTA activity.

##### Search and Filters
1. Unauthenticated users can search for properties and projects but cannot view images. If we choose to not show property images and only project images - does it really look good on the UX? Let us know exact business rules for showing images of properties and projects for unregistered and registered users? (if they choose to show images for property/if they do not wish to show images)

   **Answer:** So the business rule is to hook the audience on images, we are still showing them the card details and we want user to atleast provide mobile number to us for them to begin exploring our platform. Hence we want to blur property images and okay to show project images.

   The other logic of property images shown is solely of an agent if they want to show images, as some users are not happy to showcase their image to audience but as our platform requires images we will have to ask them to upload but listsing wise they can hide those images to show it to the end audience and they can request for images, similar to magic bricks. This helps Agents to upload more properties on the platfrom as their listings are secured. (Request based approval)

##### Property Management
1. When adding a location, how should the map work in post a property or demand? What is expected behaviour for maps? Do we paste the URL or embed link.

   **Answer:** There is no map in demand but only in property. The property map is nothing but a map of the location of property, also it will have a leaflet and also (view street view) (Map view). Property location marker, nearby bank, nearby bustop, nearby restaurant, shopping destinations etc based on the asset class), only street view will open a pop-up of street view on the same page rest user can view everthing on the map

##### Demand Management
1. Agents may receive a notification that a large demand exists in their area to keep them engaged without the CTA? This is a business rule written when we discussed previously. Can you give us more clarity on this?

   **Answer:** This is to engage with the audience for them to post more properties, they will just get to view that there are x number of demands in their area. Post your properties to get matched to the right demand.

##### Project Management

Does the link dynamically redirect to the developer's WhatsApp line, or does it route the message to the internal Keydemand admin team as a system lead? Since there is no Developer dashboard? Where does the lead go to and who all does the lead go to? Only super admin and assigned relationship manager? What is the developer's role here then?

   **Answer:**

Details of what will be asked while filling the form is already shared.
   - User who is a registered user > clicks on project interested > automatically details will be captured and the CTA will be changed to intrerest shown on this project on \<date\>, similarly details for this will be sent as above.

##### Notifications
- Marketing notifications - from Keydemand end
- New Demands Uploaded(Area Specific) - Not there presently -

1. Where will the above be redirected to? If there is anything specific eg view phone number, then it should embed the user who has viewed phone number and take the user to that page where the view phone number was done (eg)
   - **Answer:** If lead then to the lead page. If new relevancy then to the relevancy page etc
2. Agents cannot see new demands right? — **Yes agents cannot see demands, until its matched against their property**
3. Also where will marketing notifications go? Whatsapp? — **Marketing notifications will be sent via whatsapp but they will be tracked back to the website/app where users can directly go to the hyperlinked outcome or deeplinking it to the specific pages where require.**

#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-DQ-056** — Subscription is billed monthly and auto-charged on the same date each month; renews automatically. _(§ Profile #2 How billing works)_
- **BR-DQ-057** — User can cancel anytime from account settings; auto-renewal stops immediately; full premium access continues until end of the current billing cycle. _(§ If you cancel)_
- **BR-DQ-058** — If auto-payment fails, a "Renew" button is shown on the user's subscription page. _(§ If a payment fails)_
- **BR-DQ-059** — After the last successful payment, all listings stay active for 3 months; during this period the user can view leads and relevancy but cannot connect with new users. _(§ listings after cancellation)_
- **BR-DQ-060** — After those 3 months, all listings are deactivated; data is retained; on resubscription the user must manually select listings to make them active. _(§ listings after cancellation)_
- **BR-DQ-061** — Deactivating an account hides all listings and the user does not appear active on the platform. _(§ Deactivating)_
- **BR-DQ-062** — A "Reactivate account" button is available on the home page of a deactivated user; on reactivation the account is marked "registered but not subscribed". _(§ Deactivating)_
- **BR-DQ-063** — If the user deactivated during an active subscription and reactivates within the original subscription period, subscription benefits resume automatically. _(§ Note)_
- **BR-DQ-064** — Reactivation outside the subscription period makes the user a general registered user who must subscribe again / is asked to subscribe on any CTA activity. _(§ Note)_
- **BR-DQ-065** — Unregistered users see property card details but property images are blurred; project images are shown. Mobile number is required to begin exploring. _(§ Search and Filters)_

### Subscription Related Doubts  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** Google Doc · ID `10OGqoOMuOqKwcGnz8yZ7fvpmB6MM83c0MVqUkTWr5-Q` · owner pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · created/modified 2026-06-03 · sections read: items 1–4 and 1 embedded handwritten image · comments: none · read coverage: 100%

#### Content
**Subscription Related Doubts**

1. As per Subscription (Retail and F&B) is a bundle and (Office) is a bundle — **Yes**
2. We want to know more about the Prorating system - For example, if a subscription is done on 5th June, Will the subscription be for the next 25 days as the cycle begins on 1st or will the next bill be generated on 5th July? 2nd Month onwards- which date will the billing start?

   We use a **30-day billing cycle**, counted from the date you first subscribe.

   #### Example: Himanshu's account
   - **10 June** — Himanshu subscribes to 1 city + 1 asset class. His next billing date is **10 July** (30 days later).
   - **15 July** — Himanshu adds a 2nd city mid-cycle. On this date, he is charged:
     - The full amount for his existing city + asset class (10 July to 9 August)
     - A prorated amount for the new city, covering the remaining 25 days until his next billing date
   - **9 August onwards** — Both cities are billed together as part of his regular monthly cycle.

   The same logic applies when adding a new asset class.

   **In short:** Existing subscriptions renew on schedule. New additions are prorated to align with your next billing date.

   [Image: handwritten note —
   "* Subscription cycle – Date of purchase + 30 days.
   * Mid-way additional city / asset class – Pro-rated calculation: eg.
   – Original subscription date for 1 city & 1 asset class – 5th May
   – ∴ Next subscription date – 5th June
   – Additional purchase of 1 city – 25th May
   – ∴ Amt. charged for addⁿ purchase – 10 days (5th June – 25th May)
   – Next subscription on 5th June – 2 cities"]

3. If a user has subscribed for Mumbai(Retail) and Bangalore(Office) and when posting a demand, only the cities he has chosen must open in the drop down and other cities be disabled? How the UI must be? — **To show only cities the user is subscribed to.**

   How do we show the cities in the city selector? Do we lock any cities? What will be the behaviour of Asset classes? — **The user will have only the asset class selected while posting the property/demand. Eg if they have subscribed to F&B and Retail then only that to be shown while posting the property/demand. If selected both then to show F&B & Retail and Office space as asset class. Therefore we must show only cities that the user has subscribed to.**

4. Also when posting a demand/property - When they choose a location and asset class, if the user has not paid for an asset class, how the UI must be? What exactly must be disabled? Any specific business rules? — **We must only showcase the asset class that the user has paid for and not the one he has not paid. Same with the cities. The drop-down during the city will only showcase the selected city, if the user has only selected one city eg Mumbai (MMR) then while posting property/demand it will only mention Mumbai**

#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-DQ-077** — Subscription asset-class bundles: (Retail and F&B) is one bundle; (Office) is one bundle. _(§ 1)_
- **BR-DQ-078** — Billing cycle is 30 days counted from the date of first subscription (not calendar month). _(§ 2)_
- **BR-DQ-079** — Adding a city or asset class mid-cycle is charged a prorated amount for the remaining days until the next billing date; thereafter all items bill together on the original cycle date. _(§ 2, image)_
- **BR-DQ-080** — Existing subscriptions renew on schedule; new additions are prorated to align with the next billing date. _(§ 2 In short)_
- **BR-DQ-081** — When posting a property/demand, the City dropdown shows only cities the user is subscribed to (e.g. only Mumbai (MMR) if only that city). _(§ 3, § 4)_
- **BR-DQ-082** — When posting a property/demand, the Asset Class options show only paid asset classes: F&B & Retail bundle → F&B and Retail; Both → F&B, Retail and Office space. Unpaid asset classes are not shown (not merely disabled). _(§ 3, § 4)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Himanshu example is internally inconsistent: on 15 July (after the 10 July renewal) he is "charged the full amount for his existing city + asset class (10 July to 9 August)" on the same day as the add-on — suggests renewal charged on add date; also "remaining 25 days" from 15 July to 9 Aug is 25 days (OK) but the renewal for 10 July would already have been billed.
- Handwritten example: 5 May → 5 June is 31 days, not 30; prorated "10 days (5th June – 25th May)" is actually 11 days.
- Office vs Managed Offices bundle: § 1 says "(Office) is a bundle"; elsewhere bundle is "Office & Managed Spaces".
- Whether non-subscribed cities are hidden or shown-disabled: answer says "show only", question offered "disabled".

- Subscriptions are structured by city and asset class.
- Each active combination of 1 city × 1 asset class includes 5 mobile number views per month.
- Examples:
  - 1 city + 1 asset class = 5 phone views / month
  - 1 city + 2 asset classes = 10 phone views / month
  - 2 cities + 2 asset classes = 20 phone views / month
- Mobile number visibility is restricted and unlocked only within the allotted monthly limits.
- Only 1 listing will be given free post-registration
- Rejected or restricted assets remain in explore-only view
- Users can track interests submitted
- Flow View Number or Request Call Back (or any other CTA), user has to register first.

**Office Tenant Onboarding**
The tenant (Office occupier) can register on the platform and fill out their office requirements on the platform while registering. As the user has already come from Office Tenant(Occupier)(/Managed Space we wouldn't ask the user for property type and pre-fill the information as Office Tenant.

**If they select Office/Managed Offices**

**Option as Office Occupier** — If selected Office Occupier:
- Mobile number and OTP
- Name
- Company Name
- Transaction Type – Lease/Buy
- City – Drop-down with text
- Location – Text with autofill
- Carpet Area – Text
- Tick box (Also interested in Managed Offices)

**Option as Managed Offices** — If selected Managed Offices:
- Mobile number and OTP
- Name
- Company Name
- City – Drop-down with text
- Location – Text with autofill
- Number of seats – Text

After filling all the fields, the demand will be posted on the platform.

Can explore all office properties and view phone numbers. There is no restriction on viewing phone numbers **(To have reports on how many and whose numbers are viewed)**

On clicking on view phone number, it will show the phone number and trigger a WhatsApp to the supplier informing them of the tenant who viewed the phone number and their demand information

**Posting Demand** — Office tenants can only post 1 requirement on the platform after registration. They will be asked to contact us if there are more than 1 requirement. Once onboarded by us, we will provide the user with demand uploading limits.

**Broker Journey & Keydemand Journey (Occupier Preview)**
The occupier will receive a request from the supplier requesting the mobile number along with the property details, where the tenant will have the option to confirm yes/no, and they will receive notification as a reminder if not done within 24 hours. Post 72hrs, it will automatically send a WhatsApp to the supplier if no action taken, stating the tenant is not interested. If accepted, then the mobile number will be shared with the supplier and if not, then a rejection will be sent on WhatsApp.

Once broker property is matched to the relevant demand only then the broker is allowed to connect with the tenant by request phone number and trigger a WhatsApp to the Tenant informing them of the supplier has requested your phone number and their property information

**A fraud report functionality is needed if the user is Broker and acting like a tenant**

**Notification in the case of requests for phone number**
1. Immediate
2. Within 72 hours if not accepted
3. Post 72 hours it should send a message to supplier informing that the tenant is not interested

- **Project lead recipients:** Agent Dashboard Gaps → RM of the project + assigned Keydemand team + admin team; Notifications doc → assigned Keydemand team (WhatsApp/Email) + Admin team (no RM mentioned). Notifications doc is later.
- **Enterprise Solution routing:** June 1 doc premise "if in Bengaluru then Bengaluru team" (all brand types); Notifications doc → Brand (Retail & FnB) always Mumbai; city-based routing (Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Bengaluru) only for Office & Managed Spaces. Notifications doc governs.
- **High-value threshold name/value:** "Leads more than 5K" (June 1) vs "Requirements more than 5K" with admin-configurable per-city minimum (Notifications); example values 5000 and 15,000 sft; "more than" vs "= or above".
- **Area-demand notification:** Agent Dashboard Gaps lists "New Demands Uploaded (Area Specific) - Not there presently" but also answers that agents get "x number of demands in their area" engagement notifications.
- **Enterprise editability:** June 1 doc says no edit/delete/deactivate for Enterprise on front-end and asks if "completely read-only", yet also asks whether Enterprise can add/remove/deactivate and manage responses — unresolved.
- **Phone-number view for tenants:** Himanshu Discussions → office tenants have no restriction on viewing phone numbers; subscription rule → agents/users view phone numbers only after subscription (applies to agents).
- **Free listing:** "Only 1 listing free post-registration" (Himanshu) vs office tenants "only 1 requirement" (demand) — different objects; vs subscription "Unlimited property listing".
- **Image visibility:** Agent Dashboard Gaps → property images blurred for unregistered users, plus agent-controlled hide with request-based approval; June 1 doc defines Image Request Received/Requested flows consistent with this.
- **RM card:** June 1 text → CTA "Call Now Button"; reference image → "Chat with …" and "Schedule a call".

#### Business rules extracted

**Subscription & cities**
- **BR-REQ-001** — Agent subscription is priced per asset class per city: Metro ₹1000 (Retail & FnB), ₹1000 (Office), ₹2000 (Both); Non-Metro ₹750 / ₹750 / ₹1500. _(§ Subscription B2:C4)_
- **BR-REQ-002** — ROI (Rest of India) subscription is priced per asset class (not per city): ₹1000 Retail & FnB, ₹1000 Office; no "Both" price given. _(§ Subscription D2:D3)_
- **BR-REQ-003** — Pan India subscription: ₹5000 Retail & FnB, ₹5000 Office; no "Both" price given. _(§ Subscription E2:E3)_
- **BR-REQ-004** — Price period (monthly/yearly) and currency unit are not stated in the sheet. _(§ Subscription)_
- **BR-REQ-005** — Cities are classified Metro (19 cities incl. Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Pune City, Hyderabad…), Non-metro (26 incl. Ahmedabad, Jaipur … Goa cities) or ROI (1,173 rows). _(§ City tab)_
- **BR-REQ-006** — Metro cities are clubbed into combinations: MMR (Mumbai, Thane, Kalyan-Dombivali, Vasai-Virar, Mira-Bhayandar, Bhiwandi, Panvel, Ulhasnagar), NCR (Delhi, Faridabad, Gurgaon, Noida, Ghaziabad), Pune (Pune City, Pimpri-Chinchwad); Non-metro combination "Goa" (Marmagao, Panaji, Margao, Mapusa). _(§ City D4:D22, H26:H29)_
- **BR-REQ-007** — "Consider combination for clubbing of cities when user buys the subscription. But while posting they will be able to see all the cities that are clubbed." _(§ City A31)_
- **BR-REQ-008** — The Admin label is "Non Metro City", not "Tier 2". _(§ Build 1 Bugs #55)_

**Property / project input fields (visible tab "Property & Project Input Fields", dated 17-06-2026)**
- **BR-REQ-009** — Agents can upload: Retail Lease, Retail Sale, F&B Lease, F&B Sale, Office Lease, Office Sale. Keydemand can upload the same six plus Flex Property (Phase 2) and Managed Office (now "as project" on frontend). Managed Space Operator projects and Developer projects are backend (admin) uploads. _(§ P&P row 2–3 headers)_
- **BR-REQ-010** — Agent must not be able to post Managed Space. _(§ Bugs #57; Access Permissions §3)_
- **BR-REQ-011** — Form field order is given by "Add/Upload Form Order"; detail-page order by "View Page Order"; editability after posting by "Can be edited-Yes/No". _(§ P&P row 4)_
- **BR-REQ-012** — Asset Class*, City*, Location*, Transaction Type* are NOT editable after posting (Can be edited = No); all other property fields are editable. _(§ P&P rows 9–12, all agent/KD blocks)_
- **BR-REQ-013** — Images & Videos* is mandatory; multiple images; Image JPEG/JPG/PNG < 2MB each; Video MP4/MOV < 5MB each; categories same as V1 (Front Side, Interior, Exterior). _(§ P&P J6)_
- **BR-REQ-014** — Retail/F&B (and KD office) properties have a "Hide Images" toggle (Yes/No); for Agent Office Lease the V2 note is "Let user ask for Images" (image request flow). _(§ P&P H6, AZ6, CH6)_
- **BR-REQ-015** — Project Name: optional text, alphanumeric. About Property / Project*: mandatory text, alphanumeric. _(§ P&P rows 7–8)_
- **BR-REQ-016** — City*: dropdown + search, single city; Location*: search with autofill, single location. _(§ P&P rows 10–11)_
- **BR-REQ-017** — Transaction Type options Lease, Sale (radio, single select); the block determines the pre-selected value. _(§ P&P row 12)_
- **BR-REQ-018** — Carpet Area (sq. ft.)* is a number with Indian comma grouping & suffix (e.g. 2,500 sft; 25,000 sft; 1,00,000 sft). _(§ P&P row 13)_
- **BR-REQ-019** — Lease: Rate per sq. ft. (Carpet)* is auto-calculated when Quoted Rent* is provided, and Quoted Rent* is auto-calculated when the rate is provided: Rate = Quoted Rent ÷ Carpet Area; Quoted Rent = Carpet Area × Rate (example: Rent 300000, Rate 200, Area 1500). _(§ P&P rows 14–15, 68–70; CA15:CA16)_
- **BR-REQ-020** — Sale: Quoted Price* auto-calculated if Rate per sq. ft. is provided and vice-versa. _(§ P&P AK14:AK15, BG15:BG16)_
- **BR-REQ-021** — Rate per sq. ft. and Quoted Rent should work together, not with carpet area directly (bug). _(§ Bugs #4)_ — note this conflicts in wording with BR-REQ-019's formula, which uses carpet area.
- **BR-REQ-022** — On the lease side, Rate per sft must not accept more than 4 digits (example given: "2 Lakh per Monthly"). _(§ Bugs #120)_
- **BR-REQ-023** — Property Available From* (Retail/F&B/Office): Immediate, Within 3 months, Within 6 months, Within 9 months, After 9 months (dropdown, single). Flex/Managed: Immediate, 3 Months (Within 3 months). _(§ P&P row 16, ED14, FO13)_
- **BR-REQ-024** — Store Type* (Retail/F&B): Highstreet, Mall (radio, single); mandatory. _(§ P&P row 17; Bugs #12, #26)_
- **BR-REQ-025** — Retail Floor*: Basement, Upper Ground, Ground, 1st Floor, 2nd Floor, 3rd Floor, Above 3rd Floor (dropdown, single). Office Floor: 1 to 5, 5 to 10, 10 to 15, Above 15. _(§ P&P rows 19, AS23)_
- **BR-REQ-026** — Clear Ceiling Height (ft.)* and Frontage (ft.)* are numbers only with "ft" suffix (e.g. 12 Ft, 22 Ft); Frontage is mandatory for Retail/F&B lease (optional "Frontage (ft.)" on F&B Sale). _(§ P&P rows 20–21; Bugs #11, #18, #21)_
- **BR-REQ-027** — Retail: Mezzanine Available, Washroom Available*, Fitouts Available, Parking Available are Yes/No radios; Washroom is mandatory, Parking is not mandatory. _(§ P&P rows 22–25; Bugs #15, #19, #22, #23)_
- **BR-REQ-028** — OC Status*: Received, Applied, Not Available, Under Construction (dropdown, single). _(§ P&P row 26)_
- **BR-REQ-029** — Retail/F&B Amenities (multi-select tick box): AC, CCTV Surveillance, Central Air Conditioning, Facilities For Disabled, Fire Exit, Fire Fighting System, Lift, Power backup, Reserved Parking, Security Services, Lift, Signage, Vastu Compliance, Visitor's Parking. _(§ P&P row 27)_
- **BR-REQ-030** — F&B property extra fields: Cooking Type (Electric, Gas) and Non-Veg Allowed (Yes, No) — new in V2. _(§ P&P L–U rows 27–28)_
- **BR-REQ-031** — Commercials (lease): Deposit in Months (number), CAM / Maintenance Charges (number, total amount, e.g. ₹850 per month), Rent Escalation (Every Year / Every 3 Year + percentage, e.g. "Every Year 5%"), Lease Tenure in Years (number), Lock-in Period (number). _(§ P&P rows 29–33)_
- **BR-REQ-032** — Lock-in period cannot be greater than lease tenure years (property); for demand: "Lock-in period cannot be more than lease period, It can be equal or less". _(§ P&P G33; Demand G27; Bugs #5, #13)_
- **BR-REQ-033** — Google Location: map with location search and leaflet; the location should use a leaflet wrapper when a property/project is posted. _(§ P&P row 35; Bugs #115)_
- **BR-REQ-034** — Other Documents: PDF < 2MB (Keydemand block note says "Upload file should be less than 5MB in PDF format" — conflict). Add Video URL: YouTube or Vimeo link, clicking routes to YouTube/Vimeo. _(§ P&P rows 36–37, BU37; Bugs #16)_
- **BR-REQ-035** — Fields deleted from V1 for agent retail property: Builtup Area, Ownership, Brokerage in days, Age of property, Floorplans/Autocad/Fire NOC/Other licenses available, Pin Code, Negotiable. _(§ P&P D41:D50)_
- **BR-REQ-036** — V1→V2 renames (e.g. "Toilet available"→"Washroom Available", "OC available"→"OC Status*", "Number of parking spaces"→"Parking Available", "Floorplans / Autocad / Fire NOC / Other Licenses"→"Other Documents"). _(§ P&P D54:E65)_
- **BR-REQ-037** — Office property (lease/sale) fields: Built up Area (sq. ft.)*, Quoted Rent*/Quoted Price*, Rate per sq. ft. (Carpet)*, Washroom Count*, Fitouts status* (Furnished, Unfurnished, Developer/Landlord to do fitout), Bike Parking* (number), Car Parking* (number), Floor, Amenities (office list), Meeting Room (number), Cabins (number), Deposit, Lease tenure, Rent escalation, CAM. _(§ P&P AS–BM)_
- **BR-REQ-038** — Office amenities list: AC, Cafeteria/Food court, Lift, Security, CCTV Surveillance, Centralized AC, Facilities for Disabled, Fire fighting system, Fire sensors, Pantry, Reception area, Security, Service lift, Vastu Compliance, Power Backup, Fire Exit, Reserved Parking. _(§ P&P AS25)_
- **BR-REQ-039** — Carpet area should not be more than Built up area (office/KD blocks). _(§ P&P cell comments BB13, BM14, DF14, DQ14, EB14)_
- **BR-REQ-040** — Keydemand-uploaded properties have "Who can see your property*" (Office Tenant, Retail Brand, F&B Brand, Enterprise Brand, Enterprise Tenant, Keydemand, Agent) — not visible at user end; "This option should be default no, they can change it if wish to". Single select on Retail Lease KD block, Multi Select on F&B/Office KD blocks. _(§ P&P BO10, CA11, CW10)_
- **BR-REQ-041** — "Who can see your demand" must not appear when an Agent posts a property; it applies to Keydemand users only. _(§ Bugs #126)_
- **BR-REQ-042** — While uploading Keydemand properties, the toggle "not show properties to Agents" defaults ON. _(§ User Dashboard N58)_
- **BR-REQ-043** — Flex Property (Keydemand) is Phase 2: per-format rates (Flexi Desk, Dedicated Desk, Meeting Room, Cabins, Managed Office) — "At least one" rate required; Business Hours (Fixed timings, 24 hours); Bike/Car parking (Payable, Included, Unavailable); Floor Number; Age of property (Less than 5 Years, 5 - 10 Years, 10 - 20 Years, Above 20 Years); Nearest Connectivity (Railway Station, Bus Station, Metro Station); Amenities* (flex list); Brochure PDF < 2MB. _(§ P&P ED–EM)_
- **BR-REQ-044** — Managed Office (Keydemand, "As project now - frontend"): Managed Centres*, About Centre*, Transaction Type* = Lease, Asset Class* (Managed Offices, Managed Space), Number of seats*, Team size*, Lock-in period*, Price per seat*, Workspace Solution (Ready to Move, Curated Built to Suit; multi-select), Business Days and Hours (start–end time + 5/6 days a week tick, e.g. 9:00 am - 19:00 pm), Amenities. _(§ P&P EO–EX)_
- **BR-REQ-045** — Managed Office Space Project (Managed Space Operator) is uploaded from backend and "Can be edit through Admin panel only": Images & Videos*, Managed Centres*, About Centre*, Transaction Type* Lease (pre-selected), City*, Location*, Asset Class* pre-selected "Managed Office Space", Property Available From* (Immediate, 3 Months), Workspace Solution, Total Number of seats*, Meeting Rooms (Yes/No), Minimum Lock-in period*, Price per seat* (per seat/month, e.g. ₹1,850 per seat/month), Business Days and Hours, Existing Tenants, Amenities, Google Location, Brochure, Add Video URL, Assign Keydemand POC (KD team users; multiple users can be selected). _(§ P&P EZ–FJ)_
- **BR-REQ-046** — Managed Space Operator centre form: "Team Size" must not be there; "Existing tenants" field to be deleted; headers must read 'Managed Centres', 'Managed Office Format', 'Additional Details', 'Property Available From'; Description, Lock-in Period, Business Days & Hours, Workspace Solution need field boxes and validation. _(§ Bugs #127, #158–#161)_
- **BR-REQ-047** — If the asset class is managed space, transaction type must be Lease only (dynamic). _(§ Bugs #118)_
- **BR-REQ-048** — Developer Projects (backend upload; "Entire projects can be edit through Admin only"): Images & Videos*, Project Name*, Developer Name*, Location*, Project Type* (IT Parks(IT/ITES), Mixed Use, Office Building, Mall, Highstreet), Unit Size Min*/Max*, Total Project Size in sq.ft* (number in sft with dropdown carpet/built-up), Asset Class* (Retail + F&B / Mixed Use / Office), Efficiency* (%), Project Status* (Ready to Move, Under Construction), Possession Date* (MM/YY), About Project*, Total No of Parkings Available, Transaction Type* (Lease, Sale), Rera Id, Quoted Price / Quoted Rent, OC Status*, Feature & Amenities*, Brochure (PDF < 5MB), Google Location*, Age of Project (Less than 5 years, 5 - 10 years, Above 10 years), Floorplans available (PDF/JPEG/PNG < 5mb, multi-upload), Assign Keydemand POC. _(§ P&P HM–HT)_
- **BR-REQ-049** — Project Asset Class "Mixed Use" (renamed from F&B) gives relevancy from retail, F&B & offices; "Retail + F&B" shows relevancy for both. _(§ P&P HS14)_
- **BR-REQ-050** — Efficiency = usable share, e.g. 1000 sft super built-up with 500 sft carpet → 50%. _(§ P&P HS15)_
- **BR-REQ-051** — Project Quoted Rent (lease) / Quoted Price (sale), e.g. ₹1,00,000/sft or ₹150/sft; if not given show "Request for price" / "Price on enquiry". _(§ P&P HS23; Card Details O10)_
- **BR-REQ-052** — Assign Keydemand POC (dropdown: Kavan Nanaiah, Deepali, Shamli, Sohel, Nilesh, Ajay, Akhil, Raja, Yash, Prakash, Shanker, Ramesh, Dhanbal, Chetna Bhanushali, Sabeer Basha, Navaneeth, Jeevan, Rohith, Prasad Babu, Arun) is visible only at Admin end while uploading, never at user end; multiple KD team members can be assigned. _(§ P&P HS32; Bugs #86)_
- **BR-REQ-053** — If project status is Ready to Move, Possession Date must be greyed out / frozen. _(§ Bugs #108, #130)_
- **BR-REQ-054** — Do not pre-fill/pre-select any values when uploading project, property or demand; remove example placeholders. Age of property must show "Select" until chosen. _(§ Bugs #61, #107, #121, #128, #146)_
- **BR-REQ-055** — Rera ID is shown only for Agent and Developer users. _(§ Bugs #89; User Profile A14)_

**Demand input fields**
- **BR-REQ-056** — Demand forms exist for: Agent (Retail Lease/Buy, F&B Lease/Buy, Office Lease/Buy; Flex Lease marked "Agent (Remove)"); Brand (Retail Lease/Buy, F&B Lease/Buy); Brand Individual quick journey (F&B and Retail Lease/Buy during login); Office Tenant (Office Lease/Buy); Flex Tenant; Managed Space Occupier (quick + detailed journey); Keydemand (Retail Lease/Buy, F&B Lease/Buy, Office Lease/Buy, Flex (Phase 2), Managed Space). _(§ Demand rows 1–2)_
- **BR-REQ-057** — Demand Asset Class*, Transaction type*, City*, Location* are not editable after posting; other fields editable. _(§ Demand A5:A8 etc.)_
- **BR-REQ-058** — "Other interested Location": up to 3 additional locations (search with autofill). _(§ Demand G9)_
- **BR-REQ-059** — Retail demand: Carpet area in sq.ft*, Possession needed* (Immediate … After 9 months), OC required (Yes/No), Additional Demand Details (text), Floor Preference* (Ground, Any), Clear ceiling height (ft), Frontage in feet, Store type* (Highstreet, Mall, Any), Toilet/Fitouts/Parking/Mezzanine required (Yes/No), Amenities required (multi), Lease tenure in years, Lockin period. Buy variant replaces lease terms with Budget (number). _(§ Demand A–I, AG–AO)_
- **BR-REQ-060** — Floor Preference* and Store type* are mandatory on demands. _(§ Bugs #10, #25)_

- **BR-REQ-062** — Office demand: Age of property (Any, Less than 5 Years, 5 - 10 Years, Above 10 Years — Office Tenant variant: Less than 5 Years, 5 - 10 Years, 10 - 20 Years, Above 20 Years, Any), Toilet Required, Car Parking Required, Bike Parking required, Fitout Status (Unfurnished, Furnished), office Amenities. _(§ Demand AR–AZ, EE–EX)_ — Bugs #96 says Age of property should be removed per PR sheet (conflict).
- **BR-REQ-063** — Deleted demand fields from V1: Pincode, End use, Rent Budget per sq.ft, Add Brand Name, Willing to pay brokerage?, Ownership, Age of property, Required Documents. _(§ Demand D33:D41)_
- **BR-REQ-064** — Brand demand forms show "Select Brand (Formats)" only for Enterprise Brands with multiple brands; "When they are onboarded and then click post a demand, these may come". _(§ Demand BZ5, CC5, BW32)_
- **BR-REQ-065** — "Yes" fields (editable fields) cannot be edited after the demand got a response. _(§ Demand EE33, IQ29; Access Permissions §3)_
- **BR-REQ-066** — Managed Space Occupier demand: Asset Class* Managed Space, Possession needed* (Immediate, Within 3 months), Number of seats* — only accepts more than 20 seats. _(§ Demand FL–FS rows 4, 9, 10)_
- **BR-REQ-067** — Managed Space demands "would not be shown to any users except Keydemand team" and "will be sent to KD team and Admin team as a requirement". _(§ Demand FL12:FL13)_
- **BR-REQ-068** — Keydemand-posted Managed Space demands are viewed only by other Keydemand team (Explore, relevancy); no other suppliers can view them; they are also sent to other KD team and Admin team. _(§ Demand JC13:JC14)_
- **BR-REQ-069** — Keydemand-posted demands have "Who can see your demand*" (Developer, Keydemand, Agent), not visible at user end. _(§ Demand FV7, GH7)_
- **BR-REQ-070** — Flex demand formats: No. of Seats for Flexi Desk / Dedicated Desk / Meeting Room / Cabins / Managed Office, Budget per seat; Phase 2 for Keydemand; Agent Flex Lease marked Remove ("Formats (Adding one format mandatory)"). _(§ Demand IQ–IY, BN–BU)_
- **BR-REQ-071** — Flex Tenant demand has "Show Brand" checkbox (Yes/No). _(§ Demand FC3)_
- **BR-REQ-072** — Office occupier who selected "interested in managed space" at registration must be able to post both Office and Managed Office demands. _(§ Bugs #119)_
- **BR-REQ-073** — End-use reference lists: Office end use (Insurance … Tourism and Hospitality, 29 values); Retail end use (Automative showroom, Banks/ATM, Kiosk, Clinic/Diagnostic center, Clothing store, … Watch); FnB (Fine Dining, QSR & Fast Food, Cafés & Bistros, Pubs Bars & Lounges, Banquets & Event Catering, Cloud Kitchens, Cafe, Restaurant). Enterprise "End use" must be a dropdown from the provided list. _(§ Demand D61:F100; Bugs #168)_

**Search filters (New Platform Requirement-Filter)**
- **BR-REQ-076** — Customized search for Properties & Projects and for Demand: CITY, ASSET CLASS & LOCATION ARE MANDATORY. _(§ Filter E2, S1)_

Projects — Asset class (Retail + F&B, Mixed-used, Office, Managed Offices), Transaction (Lease, Sale), Total Project size slider, Project Status, Project Type, Seats slider. _(§ Filter E15–K44)_

KEYDEMAND.IN
Product Requirements Document
Platform Relaunch — All User Types & Journeys

| Version | v1.0 —  |
|---|---|
| Date | 8 April 2025 |
| Prepared by | Keydemand Product Team |
| Status | In Review — Sections marked ⚠ require input |

How to use this document: Sections marked ⚠ TBD require decisions before development begins. Sections marked 💡 contain product suggestions from the author. All TBDs should be resolved and signed off before this document moves to v1.1.

##### 1. Product Overview

Keydemand.in is a commercial real estate listing and demand-matching platform serving three asset classes: F&B, Retail, and Offices. The platform connects tenants (brands and office occupiers) with supply-side participants (agents and developers) with Keydemand operating as both a marketplace enabler and a directly managed transaction layer for enterprise and high-value requirements.
###### 1.1 Platform Model
- Tenants discover properties, submit demands, and connect with suppliers via the platform.
- Agents list properties, respond to inbound demand leads, and manage their inventory.
- Keydemand operates a privileged internal team role with full access plus the ability to manage enterprise accounts, assign leads, and curate managed office supply.
- Enterprise accounts (both tenant and brand sides) are handled with a higher-touch, offline onboarding flow that flows into the platform.
###### 1.2 User Types

| User Type | Sub-type | Asset Class | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand | Individual | F&B, Retail | Social media CTA / Direct reg. |
| Brand | Enterprise | F&B, Retail | Individual escalation / Website enquiry / KD team |
| Office Tenant | Individual / Managed | Offices | Social media CTA / Direct reg. |
| Office Tenant | Enterprise | Offices | Individual escalation / Website enquiry / KD team |
| Agent | Non-reg / Reg / Subscribed / Expired | All | Social media / WhatsApp / Website / KD team |
| Keydemand Team | Internal | All | Internal — admin dashboard |


##### 2. User Journey — Brand (Individual) · Retail & F&B (3 Requirements Free)

###### 2.1 Discovery & Entry Points
- Social media CTA (LinkedIn / Meta ad) → Registration & demand capture flow
- Direct registration → Keydemand.in registration link
###### 2.2 Registration Flow
Both entry points converge on the same registration link. Steps:
- User details — Name, mobile number (OTP)
- Single demand details — Asset class, transaction type, city, location, Carpet area, Floor
- T&C acceptance (Tick box with T&C to be on a clickable basis)
- Option: 'Enquire for Enterprise Solution' — if selected, lead is transferred to Keydemand team
###### 2.3 Post-Registration: Social Media CTA Path
When sourced via social media CTA:
- Registration & demand data captured (similar like above)
- User lands on: Microsite — Retail & F&B city-specific page showing relevancy & supply summary with option to explore property options
- If Enterprise Solution selected → lead transferred to Keydemand team
- Upon registration: 1 demand added; up to 2 more demands can be added subsequently.
💡 SUGGESTION: Consider adding a 'save my search' prompt immediately after registration so the user gets WhatsApp/email alerts when new matching properties are added — this dramatically increases return visits.
###### 2.4 User Journey (Linear)

| # | Stage | Action / Screen | Notes / TBDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Discovery | Social media / direct URL |  |
| 2 | Registration | User details + demand + T&C | 1 demand added on reg. |
| 3 | Relevancy / Explore | Microsite: city supply summary, explore property options | Retail & FnB properties can be explored |
| 4 | CTA to view contact | Contact number to be shared over WhatsApp with user + supplier notified | Number gated behind CTA |
| 5 | Dashboard | Relevancies & contact requests accessed via dashboard | See Section 2.5 |

###### 2.5 Dashboard Screens — Brand Individual
- Dashboard built on / linked from Homepage
- Profile — editable user and brand details
- Explore — property/project pages (Retail & F&B asset class)
- Request for Enterprise Solution
- Submit Demand — add up to 2 more demands post-registration
- My Demands — edit, delete, view listing performance
💡 SUGGESTION: The dashboard should surface a 'demand status tracker' — showing how many relevancies have been found, how many suppliers have viewed the demand, and how many contact requests have been made against each demand. This reduces support queries and keeps users engaged.

##### 3. User Journey — Office Tenant (Individual)-occupier

###### 3.1 Discovery & Entry Points
- Social media CTA (LinkedIn / Meta) → Registration & demand capture
- Direct registration → Keydemand.in registration link
###### 3.2 Registration Flow
- User Type selection — Office Space or Managed Space
- User details — Name, mobile number
- Single demand details (Tenant Space path) or Managed Space details If Tenant requirementTransaction type, Company name, City, Location, Carpet Area, Tick box (Also interested in managed spaces)If Managed SpaceMobile number & OTP, Name, Company name, City, Location & Number of seats
- T&C acceptance
- Option: 'Enquire for Enterprise Solution'
- If Tenant path: prompt — 'Also interested in Managed Office?'
###### 3.3 Post-Registration: Social Media CTA Path
- Registration & demand data captured
- User lands on: Microsite — Office/Managed Space city-specific page with relevancy & supply summary, option to explore properties
- If Enterprise Solution or Managed Space selected → lead transferred to Keydemand team and Keydemand admin
- If size requested is above [XYZ sq ft] in [city] → lead transferred to Keydemand team (customised handling)
- Upon registration: 1 demand added; additional demands can be added via dashboard
- WhatsApp alert to KD regional rep + entry in admin dashboard central log?
💡 SUGGESTION: Consider a size-based routing logic: <2,000 sq ft = self-serve platform only; 2,000–10,000 sq ft = platform + optional KD team touch; >10,000 sq ft = KD team managed (not visible to external agents). This protects high-value relationships.
###### 3.4 User Journey (Linear)

| # | Stage | Action / Screen | Notes / TBDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Discovery | Social media / direct URL |  |
| 2 | Registration | User type → user details → demand → T&C | 1 demand added on reg. |
| 3 | Relevancy / Explore | Microsite: office/managed supply summary for city | Blurred property cards with request for photos (Agent) |
| 4 | CTA to view contact | Contact number shared via WhatsApp with tenant + supplier notified | Supplier = agent or KD depending on size |
| 5 | Dashboard | Relevancies & contact requests via dashboard | See Section 3.5 |

###### 3.5 Dashboard Screens — Office Tenant Individual
- Dashboard built on / linked from Homepage
- Profile — editable user details
- Explore — office & managed space property/project pages
- Request for Enterprise Solution
- Submit Demand — add additional demands
- Under Dashboard: My Listings — edit, delete; Listing performance
💡 SUGGESTION: For office tenants, a 'Compare Shortlist' feature (select 2–3 properties and compare side by side on key metrics: sq ft, ₹/sq ft, locality, amenities, availability) would significantly reduce the drop-off between viewing and enquiring.

##### 4. Enterprise Journeys

###### 4.1 Brand Enterprise (Retail / F&B)
Sources
- Individual user who requested Enterprise Solution from within their individual flow
- Website direct enquiry
- Keydemand team (offline-sourced lead)
Onboarding Flow (Offline → Platform)
- Enterprise enquiry received → Admin notified
- Brand onboarding — offline (Keydemand team-led)
- Requirement collection — offline
- Account creation on platform by KD team
- Brand page creation — formats, sizes, list of preferred locations uploaded
- Multi-user account creation (if applicable)
Enterprise Features — Retail / F&B
- Handholding — dedicated KD relationship manager (RM) or transaction manager (TM)
- AI layer — Locality insights, competing/complementing brand analysis, others
- Multi-user access (if applicable)
- All features available to individual user
💡 SUGGESTION: The AI layer for enterprise brands is a strong differentiator. Locality insights could include: footfall proxies (nearby transit, anchor tenants), competing brand density, complementary brand density (for co-location value), average lease rates in the micro-market. This data set, even if initially manual, becomes the product's moat.
###### 4.2 Office Enterprise
Sources
- Individual office tenant who requested Enterprise Solution
- Website enquiry
- Keydemand team
Trigger Conditions
- Tenant self-selects 'Enterprise Solution' during registration or from dashboard
- Tenant's requirement size exceeds defined threshold (XYZ sq ft / city)
Handling
When triggered:
- Keydemand regional representative is notified
- Central log maintained in KD admin dashboard
- Large-size requirements are NOT visible in external supplier/agent relevancies
- Requirement only accessible by KD team (not agents)
Enterprise Features — Office
- RM / TM assigned
- AI layer — Locality report
- Multi-user access (if applicable)
- Handholding — end-to-end support
- All features of individual Office Tenant role
###### 4.3 Managed Office — Special Rules
- If tenant opts for Managed Space: requirement is visible only to Keydemand team — not to external agents or operators directly
- Managed Office supply is added ONLY by KD team — not by agents or operators directly
- Features for managed office accounts are similar to those of an Enterprise user
💡 SUGGESTION: Managed Office as a category could be a significant revenue stream if KD charges a placement fee or commission. Define the commercial model for this category before building the supply-side UI.

##### 5. User Journey — Agent

###### 5.1 Discovery & Entry Points
- Social media / WhatsApp
- Website registration
- Keydemand team (direct onboarding)
###### 5.2 Agent States
Agents exist in one of four states, each with different access levels:

| State | Label | Access Condition | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| ① | Non-registered | Never registered | Access landing page, open project pages, explore properties (limited) |
| ② | Registered — not subscribed | Registered, no active subscription | 1 free listing + 5 contact requests; access property page; subscribe prompt |
| ③ | Subscribed | Active subscription (city + asset class) | Unlimited listings & contact requests; full dashboard; WhatsApp alerts |
| ④ | Expired subscription | Subscription lapsed | No active actions; account deactivated after 3 months of non-renewal with listings |

💡 SUGGESTION: A grace period notification system (Whats  App + in-app) at 7 days, 3 days, and 1 day before subscription expiry would significantly reduce churn. Also consider an auto-renewal opt-in at sign-up.
###### 5.3 Agent Registration Journey
- Register / Sign up / Subscribe now — via landing page button
- User details — Name, mobile number
- Redirect to homepage (State ②)
- If 'Subscribe now': asset class + select city → payment → redirect to homepage (State ③)
Alternative path — via CTA on any screen:
- Click CTA → Register prompt → User details → Continue journey
###### 5.4 Access & Permissions Matrix

| Feature / Screen | ① Non-reg | ② Reg, not sub | ③ Subscribed | ④ Expired | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access landing page | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Explore properties | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Open property page |  | ✓ | ✓ |  |  |
| Open project page | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| CTA to contact (view number) |  | ✓ | ✓ |  | 5 requests max for ② |
| Subscribe now | ✓ | ✓ |  | ✓ |  |
| Dashboard |  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Read-only for ④? |
| Profile |  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Post property / demand |  | ✓ | ✓ |  | 1 listing max for ② |
| WhatsApp alerts |  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Inbound leads + summary |


##### 6. Keydemand Team — Internal User

###### 6.1 Features & Actions
- All actions that a subscribed agent can do
- Can access inventory of other KD team members under 'My Listings'
- Dashboard includes: My Listings, Large office space enquiries, Managed office space enquiries, Projects assigned & their leads, Listing leads (property & demand), Access to all properties & demands (Explore Demand), AI layers
###### 6.2 Keydemand Team Features and Actions
- My Listings — edit, delete, view listing performance per property
- Large office space enquiries — leads above the threshold that KD has shared with agent
- Managed office space enquiries
- Projects assigned & their leads
- Listing leads — property & demand leads
- Access to all properties & demands added by any user (Explore Demand)
- AI layers — Locality insights, Brand suggestions for a property, competing/complementing.
💡 SUGGESTION: The KD team admin dashboard should include a pipeline view (CRM-lite): all enterprise leads → stage (new / in discussion / site visit / negotiation / closed / lost) → assigned rep → last activity date. This does not need to be complex at v1 — even a simple kanban or table view would significantly improve team coordination.

##### 7. Notification & Communication System

###### 7.1 WhatsApp Notifications
WhatsApp is the primary communication channel. The following trigger events have been identified:

| Trigger Event | Recipient | Content | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tenant views contact number | Supplier / Agent | 'New enquiry on [property name]' | Agent notified about enquiry |
| Supplier shares number with tenant | Tenant | Supplier contact number shared | Number shared over WhatsApp — not shown in UI |
| New matching property added | Tenant | New relevancy alert | TBD: is this automated or manual? |
| Inbound lead on listing | Agent | Lead alert + summary | WhatsApp alert to agent |
| Enterprise enquiry received | KD Admin | New enterprise lead notification | Admin notified immediately |
| Subscription expiry approaching | Agent | Renewal reminder | TBD: 7d / 3d / 1d before? |

💡 SUGGESTION: Set up a WhatsApp Business API template for each trigger event listed above. WABA template approval takes 2–5 days — initiate this in parallel with development to avoid go-live delays.

##### 10. Product Suggestions — Summary
The following suggestions are recommendations from the document author based on the user journey design. Each is marked with its priority and effort estimate.

| # | Suggestion | Section | Priority | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 'Save my search' / alert subscription after registration | §2.3 | High | Increases return visit rate significantly; reduces drop-off |
| S2 | Demand status tracker on tenant dashboard (relevancies found, supplier views, contact requests) | §2.5 | High | Reduces support queries; increases trust in platform |
| S3 | Size-based routing: <2K sqft = self-serve; 2K–10K = platform + KD touch; >10K = KD managed | §3.3 | High | Protects high-value relationships from agent competition |
| S4 | 'Compare Shortlist' feature for office tenants (2–3 properties side by side) | §3.5 | Medium | Reduces drop-off between browse and enquiry |
| S5 | AI locality insights data set — build manually first, automate later (footfall, competing brands, avg lease rates) | §4.1 | High | Core product moat; differentiates from generic listing platforms |
| S6 | Subscription renewal reminders at 7d / 3d / 1d + auto-renewal opt-in at sign-up | §5.2 | High | Agent churn prevention; revenue retention |
| S7 | KD admin pipeline view — CRM-lite with stages, assigned rep, last activity | §6.1 | Medium | Team coordination for enterprise leads; prevents leads falling through |
| S8 | Initiate WhatsApp Business API template approvals in parallel with dev (2–5 days WABA approval) | §7.1 | Critical / Immediate | Blocking dependency for go-live if not started early |
