###### 3. End-to-end flows

###### Flow 1 — Sign up as an agent

- **Actor:** New broker.
- **Prerequisites:** A mobile number that receives SMS.

1. The visitor enters their 10-digit number and ticks the over-18 and Terms consent.
2. For an unknown number, they pick **Property Agent** on the role screen.
3. A 6-digit code arrives by SMS. They enter it. (Resend after 30 seconds. At most 3 sends in 5 minutes.)
4. The **agent profile form** opens, with the phone number locked.
   - **Required:** Full Name, City, Asset Classes (one or more), Transaction Type (lease, buy or both).
   - **Optional:** Email, About Yourself.
5. Wrong entries are shown inline: "Please enter a valid email address", and a red marker on any missing required field. A server error shows in a pop-up.
6. They submit. The account is created and they are signed in. Terms and over-18 consent are stamped with the time.
7. A success screen shows the journey **Post, Get matched, Connect, Close**, with a button to start exploring. A user who came from a listing is returned there.

**System side-effects**

- A welcome message goes out on WhatsApp and by email, with a toast and a Complete profile button.
- If the profile stays incomplete, a WhatsApp nudge and a toast follow after 24 hours, with a Complete profile button.
- The abandoned-sign-up marker is cleared.
- An email address, if given, must be real: valid format, not a disposable inbox, and a domain that accepts mail.

**Edge cases**

- The profile photo is set from **Profile**, not at sign-up. The sign-up form shows a photo picker; confirm in the running app whether the photo is saved at this step **(inferred: the server drops it at registration)**.
- States and a cities list can be added later in the profile.
- The older requirements say email is mandatory before posting. The code makes it optional and has no email-verification step.

###### Flow 2 — Log in, session and log out

- **Actor:** Returning agent.

1. The agent enters their number and consent, then the 6-digit code.
2. They land on the page they came from, or on the home page.
3. The session refreshes quietly in the background while the app is used.
4. They can log out from the profile menu. Logging out forgets the device for push alerts.

**Error messages**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Wrong code | "Invalid code." |
| Expired code | "Your code expired. Tap Resend for a new one." |
| Too many wrong tries | "Too many attempts. Request a new code." |
| Too many resends | "Please wait N seconds" or "Try again in N seconds." |
| Account removed | "This account has been removed. Contact support." |
| Deactivated by Keydemand | A login pop-up explains and asks them to contact support. |
| Deactivated by the agent | They **can** sign in, and see a "Reactivate account" prompt (see [Flow 26](#flow-26--deactivate-or-reactivate-the-account)). |

**Edge cases:** an expired session during use triggers a silent refresh. If that fails, the agent is returned to sign-in, then back to where they were. A removed account is also refused on refresh.

###### Flow 3 — Complete and edit the profile

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open **Profile**, then **Edit Profile**.
2. The profile has three groups: Personal Details, Business Details and Preferences.
3. **Editable:** name, email, profile picture, About Yourself, designation, experience, states, cities, asset classes, transaction types, company name, RERA number, "member of a realtor body" and "show other agent demand".
4. **Not editable:** mobile number (shown as "cannot be changed"), role.
5. **Rules:** RERA number allows letters, digits, "/" and "-", up to 60 characters. Designation needs at least one letter. A bad value shows an inline error. Leaving the page with unsaved changes asks "Discard your changes?", and saving asks "Save these changes?".
6. The profile photo is a JPG or PNG up to 2 MB.

**System side-effects:** changing the agent's asset classes changes what they may post. Editing cities and asset classes changes the matches, the match alerts and the new-demand alerts for those cities.

**Edge cases:** an agent who clears their email is allowed. The "show other agent demand" switch exists on the profile. What it changes on screen is not documented, so confirm it **(inferred)**.

###### Flow 4 — Notification preferences

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open **Profile, Preferences**, or the notification page.
2. Three switches: **Push**, **WhatsApp** and **Email** notifications. The notification page also has "WhatsApp Promotional Updates", separate from transactional WhatsApp.
3. Switching a channel off stops messages on that channel. In-app messages always stay.
4. The notification page also links to a Help Desk contact.

**System side-effects:** the dispatcher checks consent per channel before each message. Bounced email addresses are suppressed.

###### Flow 5 — Choose a city, search and explore

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. The agent picks a city in the header. The choice is remembered.
2. **Explore Properties** opens search for that city. They add filters: asset class, lease or buy, locality, and class-specific ranges.
3. Results show properties and projects. Photos are visible (unless the owner hid them).
4. They can search by a Keydemand listing ID or an old v1 listing number.
5. A listing is shown only if its "Who can see this" setting allows agents, and does not exclude agents.
6. Nearby cities in the same region are included in the pool.

**Edge cases:** an agent never sees demands in search. A property posted by a colleague is visible only if its audience includes agents. The agent's own properties always show.

###### Flow 6 — Save and review favourites

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Tap the heart on a property or project card or detail page.
2. Open **Saved** to see all favourites, split into properties and projects.
3. Tap the heart again to remove.

**System side-effects:** favourite counts show on the dashboard.

**Edge cases:** the old "Favorites" address redirects to Saved. There is no saved-search feature.

###### Flow 7 — Post a property

- **Actor:** Agent.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Either the free listing is unused, or the plan covers the chosen city and asset class.

1. Open **Post Property**. An agent is never redirected away from it. (Brands, tenants and occupiers are sent to Post Demand.)
2. Choose an **asset class** from the agent's registered classes. The form then shows that class's fields.
3. Fill the **primary details:** transaction type (lease or buy), city, location (a picked place or a pasted map link), carpet area and class-specific fields such as floor, ceiling height, frontage, store type, cooking type, seats, cabins, possession and fit-out.
4. Fill the **commercials:** rent or price, deposit, lock-in, lease tenure, escalation, maintenance charges.
5. Add **photos.** At least one photo in each of three groups is required: **interior, exterior and front side.** JPG or PNG, up to 5 MB each.
6. Optionally add **documents** (PDF, up to 10 MB) and **videos** (MP4 or MOV, up to 20 MB, at most 3 uploads plus 3 video links).
7. Mark any photo as **hidden** if buyers must ask for access.
8. Submit.
9. **Production:** the listing is saved as "waiting for approval". It is not live until Keydemand approves. **Test environments:** it goes live straight away.
10. A Property posted message is sent on WhatsApp and by email (property PDF attached), with a toast and a View property button, and the listing shows on the dashboard.

**Validation and errors (plain words)**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Asset class not in the agent's list | The agent's registered asset classes do not include this one. |
| Free listing used, no plan | "Free listing limit (1) reached. Activate a subscription to post more." |
| Plan does not cover the city or class | "Your subscription does not cover this city / asset class. Add coverage to post here." |
| Missing photo group | "Missing required image categories", naming the group. |
| Carpet area missing (not Managed Space) | "Carpet area is required for this asset class." |
| Managed Space with a sale | "Managed space supports lease only." |
| Deposit or lock-in out of range | Inline message (deposit up to 36 months; lock-in cannot outlast the lease). |
| Video limit | "A listing can have at most 3 uploaded videos" or "3 video links". |
| City not served | The city must be an active served city, not a region name. |
| Map pin outside the city | The pin must fall inside the chosen city or region. |

**System side-effects**

- A listing ID is assigned at creation, with an asset-class prefix.
- A free-tier agent's free-listing counter goes up by one. It is counted only after a successful save.
- A "Property posted" message goes out on WhatsApp and email (property PDF attached), with a toast and a View property button.
- The "free limit reached" notice goes out when the limit is hit (see [Flow 20](#flow-20--hit-a-free-limit)).
- Matching to demands begins. Relevant demands appear on the property page, and match alerts go out as they happen (see section 4).
- A prompt can offer to save an unfinished form as a draft ([Flow 9](#flow-9--save-and-resume-a-draft)).

**Edge cases**

- A first-time agent with no plan can post once. That one free listing is **shared** between properties and demands.
- If a subscription is active but does not cover a city, even a free listing is not used. The agent must add coverage.
- A KD-only "Who can see this" audience is dropped on agent posts. Agent listings are open to everyone.

###### Flow 8 — Edit a property

- **Actor:** Agent, as owner.

1. Open the property, then **Edit**.
2. The edit form is the same component as the post form, filled with stored values.
3. Change any allowed field and save.
4. **Locks:** after the listing receives its **first response** (an enquiry or request), four fields lock: **asset class, transaction type, city and location.** Locked fields show as read-only. Everything else, including price, stays editable.
5. A price edit merges into the stored commercials. Clearing a single price field leaves the rest alone.

**System side-effects:** a Property edited message goes out on WhatsApp and email (revised property PDF attached), with a toast and a View property button. Edits do not send the listing back for review, even for major changes **(verified: re-moderation on edit is designed but not built)**.

###### Flow 9 — Save and resume a draft

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. While posting, the agent leaves the form part-way.
2. The partial form is stored as a draft, without validation.
3. The dashboard shows "Unfinished listings, pick up where you left off".
4. Tapping a draft re-opens the form with the saved values.
5. A draft can be deleted.

**Edge cases:** the 30-day automatic draft clean-up is **not built**. Drafts stay until deleted.

###### Flow 10 — Hide photos and approve image requests

- **Actor:** Agent as owner, and any signed-in user as requester.

1. **Hide:** on a property the owner marks chosen photos as hidden (at post or edit). Visitors and other users then see "Images hidden by the owner". But keydemand team member can see the photo.
2. **Request:** a signed-in user taps **Request images**. A dialog explains: their number is shared with the owner, the owner decides, and they are told when approved.
3. **Owner is notified** on push, WhatsApp and in-app (an action-needed alert).
4. **Owner responds** from Dashboard, Leads, Image requests: **Accept** or **Reject.**
5. **On accept:** the requester can see every photo on that property from then on. They are notified.
6. **On reject:** the requester is notified. Hidden photos stay hidden.
7. The requester sees "Image request pending" while waiting and "Request approved" afterwards.

**Edge cases:** a request expires after 72 hours with no answer. A duplicate request shows "You have already sent this request". The owner cannot request their own photos. A request on a listing that has since gone inactive is closed, and the requester is told.

###### Flow 11 — Property status changes, delete and PDF

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. **Deactivate:** from the property page or dashboard. A confirm dialog titled "Deactivate Listing?" appears. The listing leaves the marketplace, and open enquiries on it are closed.
2. **Activate:** the same control reverses it. A listing that was never approved cannot be switched on ("waiting for Keydemand approval"). A reactivated listing does not need a new review.
3. **Mark sold or rented:** allowed by the system (sold or rented removes the listing from the marketplace). The web app does not show a dedicated control **(inferred)**.
4. **Delete:** "Delete Listing?" confirm. The listing is hidden everywhere (soft delete) and open enquiries close.
5. **Download PDF:** a branded property PDF is generated, then cached for repeat downloads.

**System side-effects:** linked requests on the listing close. No notification is sent for deactivating or deleting a property under the current rules (see section 4).

###### Flow 12 — Post a demand

- **Actor:** Agent, for a client or own need.
- **Prerequisites:** The free listing is unused, or the plan covers the chosen city and asset class. (Managed Space demands skip the subscription check.)

1. Open **Post Demand**. The form is shared with brands and tenants.
2. Choose the asset class, transaction type, city and interested localities (plus optional extra locations).
3. Fill the requirement: area range, budget, possession, class-specific needs, required documents at accept time.
4. Submit.
5. In production the demand waits for approval. In test environments it goes live.
6. A demand ID is created, with an asset-class prefix.

**Rules**

- A free-tier agent shares **one** free listing between properties and demands.
- A subscribed agent must post inside covered city and package pairs ("Your subscription does not cover ... add coverage to post here").
- A demand posted by an agent is exempt from high-value routing, so other agents can see it. Its audience is fixed to agents and Keydemand.
- Demands no longer expire.

**System side-effects:** a Demand posted message (in-app and push, with a toast). Matching to properties begins. The free-listing counter goes up when it applies.

**Edge cases:** an agent cannot choose the demand audience. Other agents see an agent's demand without the poster's identity, in the same way as any demand.

###### Flow 13 — Edit, deactivate, fulfil and delete a demand

- **Actor:** Agent, as owner.

1. **Edit:** same shared form. The four identity fields lock after the first response.
2. **Fulfil:** mark the requirement as met. It leaves matching.
3. **Deactivate:** pauses it. Reactivation brings it back.
4. **Delete:** soft delete.
5. Any ending of a demand closes open requests and withdraws any high-value lead tied to it.

**System side-effects:** an edit sends a Demand edited message (in-app and push, with a Changes saved toast). Deactivating, fulfilling or deleting a demand sends no notification under the current rules (see section 4).

###### Flow 14 — See matches and "% Match"

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open one of the agent's live properties. A **Relevant Demands** rail lists demands that match.
2. Each card shows a percentage match. Below 50% is hidden.
3. Opening a demand shows **requirement fields only.** There is never a poster name, brand, company, logo, picture, or any lead or view counter.
4. To get in touch, the agent sends a request (Flow 16). The poster's contact is revealed only on acceptance.
5. A demand shows only if it is live and its audience includes agents. High-value demands held by Keydemand stay hidden until released.
6. Similarly, for a demand the agent owns, rails show **Relevant Properties** and **Relevant Projects.**

**How the % is worked out:** hard filters first (live, same lease or sale, compatible asset class, same city, within 3 km of a requested location, area within 75 to 125 percent). Then weighted rows per asset class (for example Office is 40 percent location and 40 percent area). Price is not scored.

**System side-effects:** the dashboard shows counts of relevant demands, properties and projects. New matches are sent as they happen (WhatsApp, in-app, push and toast), with a View relevancy button.

###### Flow 15 — Reveal a contact number

- **Actor:** Agent, as requester.

1. Open a property or an allowed demand and tap **View number**.
2. If already revealed, it shows again at no cost.
3. The system checks the listing is live and that the agent is allowed to see it. Otherwise they see "This listing is no longer available".
4. **Subscribed and covered:** the number reveals at once.
5. **Free tier:** one of 5 free reveals is used.
6. **Free tier exhausted:** the agent sees "Free contact-request limit (5) reached, activate a subscription to continue", plus the subscribe prompt.
7. **Subscribed but not covered:** "Subscription doesn't cover this city / asset class, add coverage to unlock."
8. A pop-up shows the revealed contact.

**Paths by target**

| Target | What happens |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Property** | Immediate reveal. The owner is notified, and the agent appears as a lead on the owner's side. |
| **Demand** | Reveal goes through a request to the poster in some cases (brand demands need approval). An agent may see a demand only if its audience includes agents. |
| **Demand held by Keydemand for a brand** | The Keydemand member's number is shown under the brand's name. No approval step. |

**System side-effects**

- The free counter goes up for free reveals.
- The owner gets a "Your number was viewed" alert as it happens (WhatsApp, in-app, push and toast).
- A "free limit reached" notice goes out the first time the limit is hit, at most once per week.

**Edge cases:** an earlier reveal always stays revealed, even if the listing later changes audience. The owner of a listing is never refused. A reveal on the agent's own listing is instant and free.

###### Flow 16 — Send an enquiry or request

- **Actor:** Agent, as initiator.

1. From a property, demand or project, tap **Enquire**, **Request contact**, **Request images** or **Show Interest**.
2. The request goes to the owner. It carries the agent's name and phone number, and an optional email.
3. The agent sees the request under Dashboard, Enquiries (sent). When the owner answers a contact request, the agent is notified on WhatsApp, in-app, push and toast (View phone number). When an image request is answered, the agent is notified on WhatsApp, in-app and push (View property). Showing interest in a project gives an in-app, push and toast confirmation.
4. The request expires after 72 hours if nobody answers.

**Types of request**

| Type | Purpose | On accept |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Property enquiry | Contact a property owner | Both sides see each other's contact |
| Demand match | Offer a property to a demand | Both sides see each other's contact |
| Image request | Ask for hidden photos | Photos unlocked |
| Project enquiry | Contact a developer | Both sides see each other's contact |
| Contact request | A "View number" that needs approval | Number revealed |
| Project interest | "Show Interest" on a project | Goes to the Keydemand project owner |

**Errors:** "You have already sent this request." "Cannot create an enquiry on your own listing." "This listing is no longer available."

###### Flow 17 — Answer received requests

- **Actor:** Agent, as owner.

1. An image request arrives as an alert on WhatsApp, in-app and push, with a Review request button. Other received requests show in Leads; the current rules have no agent alert for them.
2. Open Dashboard, Leads (received). Filter by contact requests, image requests, status.
3. **Accept:** contact is shared, or photos are granted. The requester is told.
4. **Reject:** the requester is told. Nothing is shared.
5. If nobody acts for 72 hours, the request expires.

**Edge cases:** only the recipient (or Keydemand) can accept or reject. A request cannot change after it is accepted, rejected, expired or closed. A listing that ends first closes its requests.

###### Flow 18 — Leads and "numbers viewed"

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Each property page has a **Leads** area, split into contact requests and image requests.
2. The dashboard shows "Numbers you've viewed" (outbound) and "phone numbers viewed" (inbound, other users who revealed the agent's number).
3. Projects the agent enquired about are listed under "Projects enquired".

###### Flow 19 — Notifications centre

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open **Notifications** (the bell shows an unread count).
2. Each row has a message and, where relevant, a button (for example "View phone number", "Review request").
3. Mark one read, or **Mark all read.**
4. Empty state: "You're all caught up. New alerts will appear here."
5. Error state: "Couldn't load notifications. Something went wrong. Please try again."

**Edge cases:** notifications are fetched when the page opens, not pushed live. Only events with an In-app channel in section 4 land here. Toasts (for example welcome, property posted, subscription activated) are not stored, and WhatsApp-only alerts (for example new demands in your cities) do not appear here. Push alerts reach a phone only if a device token is registered at sign-in.

###### Flow 20 — Hit a free limit

- **Actor:** Free-tier agent.

1. The agent uses up the one free listing, or the five free reveals.
2. The action is refused with a clear message (see Flows 7, 12 and 15).
3. A paywall pop-up explains the benefits: unlimited listings, unlimited number reveals, priority matching, priority placement and lead insights.
4. A **"Free limit reached"** message is sent on WhatsApp, in-app, push and toast when the free listing is used up (email still to be decided), with a Subscribe button. The new rules have no message for running out of free reveals. It is sent at most once a week per limit.
5. The pop-up offers **Subscribe**, which opens the plan builder (hidden on iOS).

###### Flow 21 — Subscribe, pay and activate

- **Actor:** Registered agent.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in as an agent, on Android or web, with an active account.

1. Open **Subscription** (or follow a paywall button).
2. Pick **cities** (Metro, Non-Metro, Rest of India, or Nationwide) and a **package**: Retail & F&B, Office, or both.
3. The summary shows the subtotal, 18% GST and the monthly total. Pan-India and Rest of India act as wildcards, and a wildcard covers its member cities. Cities in the same region are charged once.
4. Tap **Subscribe**. An order is created, then the Razorpay checkout opens.
5. The agent pays.
6. **On success:** payment is confirmed both by the app's return and by Razorpay's own confirmation. Coverage starts for 30 days. A Subscription activated message goes out on WhatsApp and by email (GST invoice PDF attached), with a toast and an Upload listing button.
7. **On failure:** the order stays unpaid. No notification is sent for a failed checkout; the Payment failed alert in section 4 covers auto-renewal only. The agent can retry. A "Your payment window was closed" message appears if checkout was abandoned.
8. A background check every 30 minutes settles a payment that succeeded but was not recorded.

**Rules**

- An agent can hold only **one** active subscription. A second purchase is refused: use add coverage, renew or cancel instead.
- A deactivated account cannot subscribe. The page explains whether the agent can reactivate, or must contact Keydemand.
- Managed Space cannot be bought.

**System side-effects:** listings that were hidden because of an earlier lapse come back when a plan is activated or renewed. The agent's state becomes "subscribed". The dashboard "Agent Subscription" banner disappears.

###### Flow 22 — Add or remove coverage

- **Actor:** Subscribed agent.

1. **Add now (paid):** the agent picks extra city and package pairs. A **prorated** quote shows the cost for the rest of the cycle only. They pay. The new coverage starts at once, and the cycle end date does not change. This purchase clears a pending cancellation.
2. **Remove:** removal is queued for the next cycle. The agent cannot remove everything: they must cancel instead. Removing a pair that is not held is refused.
3. A **next-month preview** shows what the next bill will be after pending changes.
4. Every change sends a "Plan changed" message on WhatsApp and by email (PDF invoice attached where applicable), with a toast and an Upload listing button.

**Edge cases:** an addition already covered by a wildcard or region shows a zero cost. If every addition is already held, nothing is charged, and no message is sent.

###### Flow 23 — Renew, cancel, reactivate and expiry

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. **Renew:** the plan auto-renews at the end of each cycle and charges for the merged coverage, including queued adds and removals, unless the agent turns auto-renew off. About 7 days before expiry an expiry notice is sent, and 3 days before a renewal reminder (both on WhatsApp, email, in-app and push). If the payment fails, a Payment failed alert asks the agent to update the payment method within [X] days.
2. **Cancel:** the plan stays active until the cycle ends, then pauses. A banner reads "Cancellation scheduled. Your plan stays active until [date]." A cancellation message is sent, with the last invoice.
3. **Reactivate (undo a cancellation):** while the plan is still active, the agent can undo the cancel.
4. **Cancelled then expired:** a cancelled plan cannot be renewed. The agent buys a fresh plan.
5. **Expiring soon:** the plan shows this state for the final 7 days.
6. **Expiry:** when the cycle ends without renewal, the plan becomes expired. A nightly job hides the agent's listings from the marketplace. A "Subscription expired" alert is sent (WhatsApp, email, in-app and push). The free limits apply again. Renewing or activating again unhides the listings.

**Edge cases:** deactivating the account does not unhide listings that the expiry job hid. They return only when the plan is renewed.

###### Flow 24 — My Plan, invoices and payment history

- **Actor:** Subscribed or lapsed agent.

1. Open **My Plan** to see coverage, cities, packages, renewal date and free-tier counters (free listing used, contact views used).
2. A **GST invoice** is ready to download after payment. It lists the subscriber, billing period, coverage lines and the price breakdown.
3. **Payment history** lists each payment and renewal bill.
4. An expired agent sees their previous coverage and an invoice from the lapsed plan.

**Edge cases:** the invoice PDF is always freshly produced, not cached. On iOS this page shows the plan and invoices only, with no buying options.

###### Flow 25 — Relationship manager and help requests

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. A relationship manager card exists only for enterprise brands, enterprise tenants and the RM-only roles. **Agents do not have one**.
2. Agents get help through the Contact page and FAQs. The notification page links to the Help Desk.
3. **Request help from my RM** is an enterprise feature and is not available to agents.

###### Flow 26 — Deactivate or reactivate the account

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open **Profile, Account, More**, then **Deactivate.**
2. The account is switched off. Listings and demands go down, with their open requests and any high-value lead.
3. The agent can still **sign in** to reactivate. All other writes are refused until they do. A banner and an "Account deactivated" gate explain this.
4. **Reactivate:** the listings and demands that this deactivation hid come back.
5. A Keydemand-initiated deactivation is different: the agent cannot sign in and is told to contact support.

**Edge cases:** listings hidden by an expired subscription stay hidden after reactivation, until the plan is renewed. A subscription cannot be bought while deactivated.

###### Flow 27 — Request account deletion

- **Actor:** Agent.

1. Open **Profile, Delete Account**, or the public Delete Account page. The page explains what is **taken offline** and what is **retained where required**.
2. Confirm the request. It is queued for Keydemand review, not wiped at once. Every message says "request".
3. The agent can **withdraw** the request ("Cancel your deletion request?") while it is pending.
4. A request already sent returns the same pending state.

**Edge cases:** a signed-out person can email the grievance officer instead.

---

###### 4. Notifications

**Channel key:** In-app = notification centre. Push = phone alert. WA = WhatsApp. Email = email. Toast = short on-screen message, not stored. "Notification" in the rules sheet means In-app and Push. Daily cap counts push, WhatsApp and email only. In-app and toast are exempt.

| Event | When it fires | Channels | CTA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Welcome** | First time an agent registers on the platform | WA, Email, Toast | Complete profile |
| **Profile incomplete** | 24 hours after sign-up with an incomplete profile | WA, Toast | Complete profile |
| **Free listing available** | Free plan, with free listing(s) still left | In-app, Push, Toast | — |
| **Free plan exhausted** | Free listing limit used up | WA, In-app, Push, Toast (Email to be confirmed) | Subscribe |
| **Upsell prompt (not subscribed)** | Agent tries an action without an active subscription | Toast only, not stored | — |
| **Subscription activated** | Payment succeeds and the plan starts | WA, Email (PDF invoice attached), Toast | Upload listing |
| **Plan changed or cancelled** | Auto-renew turned off, plan cancelled or plan changed | WA, Email (PDF invoice attached where applicable), Toast | Upload listing |
| **Subscription about to expire** | About 7 days before the expiry date | WA, Email, In-app, Push | View details |
| **Renewal in 3 days** | 3 days before the expiry date | WA, Email, In-app, Push | View details |
| **Subscription expired** | Plan lapses without renewal; listings are paused | WA, Email, In-app, Push | Subscribe |
| **Payment failed** | Auto-renewal payment is declined | WA, Email, In-app, Push | Subscribe |
| **Property posted** | Agent posts a property (listing PDF generated) | WA, Email (property PDF attached), Toast | View property |
| **Property edited** | Agent edits a property | WA, Email (revised property PDF attached), Toast | View property |
| **Demand posted** | Agent posts a requirement | In-app, Push, Toast | — |
| **Demand edited** | Agent edits a requirement | In-app, Push, Toast | — |
| **New properties match your demand** | A new property matches a requirement the agent posted | WA (count of matches), In-app, Push, Toast | View relevancy |
| **New demands match your property** | A new requirement matches a property the agent listed | WA (count of matches), In-app, Push, Toast | View relevancy |
| **Your number was viewed** | Someone views the agent's number on a listing (daily lead signal) | WA, In-app, Push, Toast | View phone number |
| **Contact request answered** | Owner approves or declines the agent's request to view a number | WA, In-app, Push, Toast | View phone number |
| **Image request received** | Someone requests to view the agent's hidden images | WA, In-app, Push | Review request |
| **Image request answered** | Owner approves or declines the agent's image request | WA, In-app, Push | View property |
| **Project interest shown** | Agent shows interest in a project | In-app, Push, Toast | — |
| **New demands in subscribed cities** | New requirements posted today in cities the agent subscribed to | WA | Upload properties |
| **New demands in onboarding city (not subscribed)** | New requirements in the city added at onboarding, agent not subscribed | WA | Upload properties |

**Removed from the earlier version (not in the current rules):** property deactivated or deleted, demand deactivated or deleted, request closed or listing unavailable, listing is 90 days old, and the 6 pm daily summary. Matches, number views and new city demands are now sent directly instead of through the digest.

**Open points in the rules:** Free plan exhausted has no Email decision. The 7-day "about to expire" copy is the same as the 3-day renewal copy. Contact request answered has no declined text for the notification. The payment failed CTA says "Subscribe" rather than "Update payment method".

**Not sent to agents:** contact request received (brands), project interest received (developers and Keydemand), enterprise help and assignment (Keydemand), brand and occupier upsells.

---

###### 5. Limits and rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free listings | **1 in total**, shared across properties and demands |
| Free contact reveals | 5 in total, over the account's lifetime |
| Subscription packages | Retail & F&B, and Office |
| Subscription price per package per city, per month | Metro ₹1,000; Non-metro ₹750; Rest of India ₹1,000; Pan-India ₹5,000 |
| GST | 18%, added on top |
| Billing cycle | 30 days. Auto-renews at the end of each cycle unless the agent turns auto-renew off. If an auto-renewal payment fails, the agent has [X] days to update the payment method (to be decided). Note: this follows the new notification rules; the current build has no auto-debit (see Flow 23 and section 7) |
| Expiring-soon window | 7 days |
| Renewal reminder | 3 days before the expiry date (plus a 7-day expiry notice) |
| Plans held at once | 1 |
| Mid-cycle add | Prorated for the remaining days. Cycle date unchanged. |
| Coverage removal | Takes effect next cycle. Cannot remove all. |
| Cancellation | Plan runs to the end of the cycle. |
| Photos | JPG or PNG, up to 5 MB, at least one each of interior, exterior and front side |
| Documents | PDF, up to 10 MB |
| Videos | MP4 or MOV, up to 20 MB, up to 3 uploads and 3 links |
| Profile picture | JPG or PNG, up to 2 MB |
| Identity lock | Asset class, transaction type, city and location lock after the first response |
| Request expiry | 72 hours |
| Match visibility | 50% and above, within 3 km, same city |
| Managed Space posting | Lease only. Not subscription-eligible. |
| Listing audience for agent posts | Open to everyone (the audience control is for Keydemand posts only) |
| Demand audience for agent posts | Agents and Keydemand |
| Daily digest | None. Matches, number views and new city demands are sent as they happen (see section 4) |
| One-time code | 6 digits, 30-second resend gap, at most 3 sends in 5 minutes |

---

###### 6. Coverage checklist

**Web app routes covered:** Sign-in (Phone, Verify, Role, Register, Success), Home, Search, Explore Properties, View all properties, Property detail, Property post, Property edit, Demand post, Demand edit, Demand detail, Project detail, Dashboard, Profile, Profile edit, Saved, Notifications, Subscription, My Plan, Enterprise Solution, List your project, Delete account, Contact, FAQs, Cookie settings, Menu, Account, old v1 redirects, and the redirects for Favorites, Properties, Projects, Demands, Agents and Enterprise.

**Core API areas covered:** auth, users (profile, deactivate, reactivate, deletion request, devices), properties, demands, enquiries, contact unlock, subscriptions (pricing, orders, verify, coverage, cancel, reactivate, invoices, payments, previews), notifications, favourites, drafts, dashboard, home and leads, search, documents (PDF), upload, geo, assistance and webhooks (Razorpay).

**Not applicable to agents:** the Keydemand team routes, enterprise Formats and enterprise help requests, project creation, and Leads.

- **BR-PD-0505** — On iOS My Plan shows the plan and invoices only, with no buying options. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 24 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-0506** — A relationship manager card exists only for enterprise brands, enterprise tenants and the RM-only roles; agents do not have one. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 25 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-0507** — Agents get help through the Contact page and FAQs; "Request help from my RM" is an enterprise feature not available to agents. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 25 steps 2-3)_
- **BR-PD-0508** — Account deactivation is at Profile, Account, More, Deactivate; listings and demands go down with their open requests and any high-value lead. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 26 steps 1-2)_
- **BR-PD-0509** — A self-deactivated agent can still sign in to reactivate; all other writes are refused until they do, with a banner and an "Account deactivated" gate. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 26 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-0510** — Reactivating restores the listings and demands that the deactivation hid. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 26 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-0511** — A Keydemand-initiated deactivation blocks sign-in and tells the agent to contact support. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 26 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-0512** — Listings hidden by an expired subscription stay hidden after reactivation until the plan is renewed; a subscription cannot be bought while deactivated. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 26 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-0513** — Delete Account (Profile, Delete Account or the public page) explains what is taken offline and what is retained where required. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 27 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-0514** — A deletion request is queued for Keydemand review, not wiped at once, and every message says "request". _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 27 step 2)_
- **BR-PD-0515** — The agent can withdraw a pending deletion request ("Cancel your deletion request?"). _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 27 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-0516** — A deletion request already sent returns the same pending state. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 27 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-0517** — A signed-out person can email the grievance officer instead of using the in-app deletion request. _(§ 3. End-to-end flows › Flow 27 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-0518** — Daily cap counts push, WhatsApp and email only; in-app and toast are exempt. _(§ 4. Notifications › Channel key)_
- **BR-PD-0519** — "Notification" in the rules sheet means In-app and Push. _(§ 4. Notifications › Channel key)_
- **BR-PD-0520** — Welcome fires the first time an agent registers; channels WA, Email, Toast; CTA Complete profile. _(§ 4. Notifications)_
- **BR-PD-0521** — Profile incomplete fires 24 hours after sign-up with an incomplete profile; channels WA, Toast; CTA Complete profile. _(§ 4. Notifications)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Dashboard tab set was read from the page definition; the order should be confirmed in the running app (inferred).
- Whether the profile photo is saved at sign-up is unconfirmed (inferred: the server drops it at registration), while the sign-up form shows a photo picker.
- Older requirements say email is mandatory before posting; the code makes it optional (contradiction between sources).
- What the "show other agent demand" profile switch changes on screen is not documented (inferred).
- Mark sold or rented is allowed by the system but the web app shows no dedicated control (inferred).
- Re-moderation on edit is designed but not built, so edits never return to review.
- The 30-day automatic draft clean-up is not built.
- "Free plan exhausted" notification has no Email decision (to be confirmed); the new rules have no message for running out of free reveals.
- The 7-day "about to expire" copy is the same as the 3-day renewal copy.
- "Contact request answered" has no declined text for the notification.
- The Payment failed CTA says "Subscribe" rather than "Update payment method".
- The grace period "[X] days" to update the payment method after a failed auto-renewal is to be decided.
- Current build has no auto-debit, while the new notification rules describe auto-renewal charging (Flow 23 and section 7 referenced; section 7 lists no such note, only sources).
- The Billing cycle row says auto-renew applies, but the current build has no auto-debit, so auto-renewal behaviour as built is unclear.
- No notification is sent for a failed checkout; Payment failed covers auto-renewal only.
- The Flow 15 "Demand" row says reveal goes through a request "in some cases", without stating all cases.
- Section 1 says a free-tier agent's paywall prompts "priority matching, priority placement and lead insights" as benefits; no rule elsewhere defines these.

#### Content
##### Persona 03 — Brand (Retail and F&B), Individual and Enterprise

---

###### 1. Persona Snapshot

###### Who they are

A **Brand** is a retail chain or a food-and-beverage (F&B) operator looking for stores or outlets. Retail and F&B brands share one role. The brand's own asset class (Retail or F&B) is fixed at sign-up.

| | Individual Brand | Enterprise Brand |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **How they join** | Self-serve: phone number, one-time code, one short form | Set up offline by the Keydemand team (usually after the free limit, a website enquiry, or sales outreach) |
| **Who logs in** | One person | Several people, each with their own mobile number |
| **Demands** | 3 free in total, then an Enterprise pitch | Unlimited |
| **Contact reveals** | 5 free, then an Enterprise pitch | Unlimited |
| **Saved formats and sub-brands** | Not available | Available. The brand picks "Post for" a sub-brand or the umbrella brand |
| **Relationship Manager** | None | A dedicated Keydemand manager, shown on the profile |
| **WhatsApp and email** | On (can be switched off) | Always off. In-app and push only |
| **Deactivate or delete own account** | Yes | Not allowed. Contact the Relationship Manager |

###### Goals

- Post what space the brand needs, once, and get matched properties and projects.
- Reach the right broker or landlord quickly.
- Keep sensitive requirements away from competing brokers where Keydemand takes them over.

###### What a Brand can and cannot do

| Can | Cannot |
| :---- | :---- |
| Post demands in **its own asset class** (Retail brand posts Retail, F&B brand posts F&B) | Post properties |
| Explore properties in Retail, F&B **and Office** | Explore Managed Space properties |
| Browse and show interest in projects | Browse other people's demands (Keydemand staff only) |
| Reveal supplier phone numbers (5 free) | Buy an agent subscription (agents only) |
| Request hidden photos from owners | Open the Leads page (Keydemand staff only) |
| Approve or decline contact requests on its own demands | Change its asset class after sign-up |
| Save properties and projects | Choose who can see its demand (fixed: agents and Keydemand) |

###### Limits and paywalls at a glance

| Limit | Individual | Enterprise |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 3 for the whole brand, for life. The first one is posted at sign-up | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 for life | Unlimited (counter not used) |
| What happens at the limit | A full-screen prompt to explore Enterprise Solution | Not applicable |

###### Asset-class scope

| Action | Retail brand | F&B brand |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Post a demand** | Retail only | F&B only |
| **Explore properties and projects** | Retail, F&B, Office | Retail, F&B, Office |
| **Cannot see** | Managed Space | Managed Space |

---

###### 2. Screen and Navigation Map

###### Where the menu items appear

| Surface | Items shown to a Brand |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Desktop top bar** | Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Desktop profile menu** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications |
| **Phone drawer** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications, Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Phone bottom bar** | Home, Explore, Dashboard, Menu |
| **Menu tab (mobile app)** | Explore properties, Projects, Saved, Post Demand, Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager, Notifications, Enterprise Solution, About Us, Our Clients, Investors, Contact Us, FAQs, Privacy, Terms, Cookie Policy |

**Never shown to a Brand:** Post Property, Explore Demands, Subscription, Leads, Agent Subscription, List Project (guests only).

###### Screens

| Screen | Purpose | Gate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Home | City-based feed: featured projects, new properties, exclusive projects, developer projects | Public |
| Search / Explore | Properties and projects with filters | Public (photos hidden when signed out) |
| Property detail | Full listing, contact reveal, request photos, PDF, save | Public (limited) |
| Project detail | Brochure, units, Show Interest, PDF, save | Public (limited) |
| Post Demand | The shared requirement form | Signed in. Blocked by the limit prompt when the free demands are used |
| Demand detail | Own demand, matches, edit, deactivate, delete, PDF, share link | Owner (or account team for enterprise) |
| Dashboard | Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries tabs | Signed in |
| Saved | Saved properties and projects | Signed in |
| Notifications | Notification centre | Signed in |
| Profile and Edit Profile | Details, notification switches, deactivate, delete | Signed in |
| Enterprise Solution | Enquiry form | Public. **Hidden inside the iPhone app** |
| Delete Account | Deletion request form | Signed in |
| Contact, FAQs, About, Our Clients, Investor Relations, Privacy, Terms, Cookie settings | Information pages | Public. FAQs hidden inside the iPhone app |

###### Mobile versus desktop

- The profile is a full page on desktop and a drawer entry on phones.
- The iPhone app hides every sales message (Enterprise Solution, FAQs, upgrade buttons). A limit prompt shows the limit only, with a Close button.
- Push notifications exist only in the mobile apps. The Profile page shows the push switch only there.

---

###### 3. End-to-End Flows

###### Flow 1 — Sign up as a new Brand

- **Actor:** A new brand representative.
- **Prerequisites:** An Indian mobile number that can receive SMS. Nobody has registered with it before.

**Steps**

1. Open **Sign in** ("Welcome aboard"). Enter the 10-digit mobile number. Tick the box accepting the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
2. **Continue** stays grey until both are done. Pressing it anyway explains why: "Enter your mobile number." / "Enter a valid 10-digit number." / "Please accept the Terms of Use & Privacy Policy to continue."
3. The system finds no account. The **Choose your role** screen appears with four cards: Property Agent, Retail Brand, F&B Brand, and Office / Managed Space Tenant.
4. Pick **Retail Brand** or **F&B Brand**. The card lists the free benefits: post a demand, contact up to 5 brokers, shortlist, relevancy results.
5. A six-digit code is sent by SMS. Enter it. The code submits itself when you enter the sixth digit. Pasting works.
6. The **Post your space requirement** form opens (see the field table below). Fill every starred field.
7. Tick the consent box and submit. If a required field is empty, a pop-up lists exactly which ones.
8. The system checks the chosen location **before** creating the account. If it is in another city, the pop-up "Check the location" says: "[Place] is in [City], outside [Selected city]. Pick a location inside [Selected city]." Nothing is created yet.
9. The account and the first demand are created together. The brand lands on the **You're in!** screen: "Your requirement has been posted. Our team will match you with verified properties." The button reads **See matches for your requirement**.

**Registration form fields (Brand)**

| Field | Required | Notes |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Brand Name | Yes | Shown on the demand if the brand chooses to show its name |
| Your Name | Yes | Contact person |
| Official Email ID | Yes | Checked for format, disposable domains and a working mail server |
| Transaction Type | Yes | Lease or Buy |
| City | Yes | Picked from the served cities |
| Location / Area | Yes | Picked from a map search. Must sit inside the city |
| Carpet Area (sq. ft.) | Yes | One number. The system stores it as a range with the same minimum and maximum |
| Other nearby localities | No | Up to three extra localities in the same city |
| Store Type | Yes | One choice: Highstreet or Mall |
| Floor Preference | Yes | Ground or Any |
| Possession Needed | Yes | Immediate, Within 3, 6 or 9 months, After 9 months |
| Terms consent | Yes | Required to continue |

**System side-effects**

- A **company** and **brand** record are created behind the scenes. The brand is marked Individual and tied to Retail or F&B.
- If the brand name already exists, a toast appears: "Your brand name matches a brand already on Keydemand — our team will verify your brand details shortly." The account still works.
- WhatsApp updates and all notification types start switched on.
- The first demand is posted to **Agents and Keydemand team**. It uses up **one of the three free demands**.
- A **Welcome** message goes out (in-app, WhatsApp, email).
- If the user leaves after the code but before the form, a **Profile incomplete** WhatsApp reminder goes out 24 hours later, and the number is remembered as a half-finished sign-up.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Wrong code | "That OTP is incorrect. Check the code and try again." |
| Old code | "Your code expired. Tap Resend for a new one." |
| Too many wrong codes | "Too many attempts. Request a new code." |
| Asking for a code too soon | "Please wait N seconds before requesting another OTP." The button counts down |
| Many requests | "Too many OTP requests. Try again in N seconds." |
| Registration session expired | "Your registration session has expired. Start again." |
| Number already registered | "An account with this mobile number already exists. Sign in instead." |
| Account created but demand failed | Green screen, then a yellow note: "Your account is ready, but your requirement was not saved. Post it again to start getting matches." Button: **Post your requirement** |
| Resuming an abandoned sign-up | The brand is asked to choose Retail or F&B again, because only "Brand" was remembered |
| Enterprise brand tries to self-register | Not allowed. The brand is told to use Enterprise Solution |

---

###### Flow 2 — Sign in (returning Brand)

- **Actor:** An existing brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** An active account.
1. Enter the mobile number and accept the consent tick. Continue.
2. A six-digit code arrives. Enter it.
3. The user lands on the page they came from, or on Home.
4. Sessions refresh quietly. After a long idle period the user is asked to sign in again: "Your session has expired. Please sign in again."

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand switched off by Keydemand | "This brand account has been deactivated. Contact Keydemand for help." (the brand's own users are refused until Keydemand restores the brand) |
| User deactivated it themselves | A pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now** |
| Keydemand deactivated the account | A pop-up asks the user to contact support |
| Account deleted | "This account has been removed. Contact support." |

---

###### Flow 3 — Post a demand (the full form)

- **Actor:** A brand user (individual, or enterprise team member).
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Free demands remain (individual), or the brand is enterprise.

**Steps**

1. Open **Post Demand**. The system first checks the free allowance. If it is used, the limit prompt appears instead of the form (Flow 4).
2. The page shows a progress meter and these sections. The asset class is **locked** to the brand's own class.
3. Fill the **Primary Details**, **Additional Details**, **Amenities** and (for lease) **Transaction** sections.
4. Optional: save a draft. Leaving with unsaved changes asks "Save your draft before you go?". A returning user sees "Draft restored" with **Discard draft** and **Dismiss**.
5. Press **Post Retail Demand** or **Post F&B Demand**. A pop-up lists any missing required fields.
6. A confirmation toast says the requirement is live. The demand opens in the dashboard.

**Field groups by asset class**

| Group | Retail (lease) | Retail (buy) | F&B (lease) | F&B (buy) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Format (enterprise only)** | Sub-brand pick | Same | Same | Same |
| **Primary Details** | Transaction type, City, Location, Other interested locations (up to 3), Map link (optional), Carpet area, Possession needed, OC required | Same, plus **Budget** | Same as Retail lease | Same as Retail buy |
| **Additional Details** | Ceiling height (ft), Frontage (ft), Store type, Floor preference, Show my name, Extra notes (optional) | Same | Same | Same |
| **Amenities** | Fit-outs required, Washroom required, plus the amenity picker. Brand lease form leaves out Parking and Mezzanine | Fit-outs, Washroom, Parking, Mezzanine, amenities | Fit-outs, Washroom, Parking, Non-veg served, Cooking type (Electric, Gas, Either), kitchen amenities | Same as F&B lease |
| **Transaction** | Lease tenure (years), Lock-in (years) | Not shown | Lease tenure, Lock-in | Not shown |
| **Documents** | Not shown | Required documents: Floor Plan, Autocad, Fire NOC, Other Licenses | Not shown | Required documents (same four) |

**Rules on the form**

- **Required:** Transaction type, City, Location (picked from the map list), Carpet area, Possession needed, Store type, Floor preference. For lease, the lock-in cannot be longer than the lease tenure: "Lock-in cannot be more than the lease tenure of N years."
- **Show my name on this demand:** Off by default. The form shows the live preview "Posted by [Brand name]" or, when off, "Posted by Retail Brand" / "Posted by F&B Brand". The brand name must exist in the profile to be used.
- **Amenities:** Retail and F&B share one amenity list. The picker shows how many are selected.
- **Audience:** A Brand cannot pick who sees the demand. It is always shown to **agents and the Keydemand team**. Any attempt to change it is ignored.
- **Demand card picture:** The brand's logo if one is uploaded. Otherwise a stock picture for the asset class.

**System side-effects**

- One free demand slot is used (individual brands).
- The demand is checked for **high-value routing** (Flow 15).
- A **Requirement posted** receipt appears (in-app, not counted in any daily cap).
- **Production:** the demand waits for Keydemand approval before it is live and matched. Test environments approve automatically.
- Matching starts as soon as the demand is live (Flow 16).

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand tries the other asset class | "Your account cannot post this type of demand." |
| Buy and managed space | Not applicable to brands |
| Draft exists | Offered back on the next visit |
| Duplicate or conflicting values | The form shows each problem beside its field, all at once |
| Format picked by an individual brand | Prompt: "Formats are an Enterprise feature" |

---

###### Flow 4 — Hit the free demand limit and the Enterprise pitch

- **Actor:** An individual brand with three demands used.
- **Prerequisites:** Free allowance used up.
1. The brand opens **Post Demand**. The page does not open. A prompt stands in front.
2. The prompt says the account includes three free demands and pitches unlimited postings, priority matching with landlords and a dedicated Relationship Manager.
3. Buttons: **Explore Enterprise Solution** and **Back to Dashboard**.
4. If the brand tries through another route, the server refuses: "Free brand limit (3 demands) reached. Upgrade to Enterprise to post more."
5. An in-app message also appears: "You have used all 3 requirements on your plan. Enroll for Enterprise Solution to post more." with an **Enroll** button.

**Rules**

- The count belongs to the **brand**, so every user under the brand shares it.
- It never goes back down. Deleting a demand does not return a free slot. The delete screen says so.
- Enterprise brands skip this check.
- Inside the iPhone app the prompt shows the limit only. There is no upgrade button.

---

###### Flow 5 — Enquire for Enterprise Solution

- **Actor:** Any visitor or brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Not available in the iPhone app.
1. Open **Enterprise Solution** from the menu or from the limit prompt.
2. Fill: Full Name (required), Company (required), Work Email (optional, checked if given), WhatsApp Number (required, +91 fixed), Primary City Focus, Brand Type (Retail, F&B, Office or Managed Space).
3. Press **Submit Enquiry**. A **Thank you for your enquiry** panel replaces the form, with **Submit another enquiry**.
4. Errors: "Couldn't submit your enquiry — please try again."

**System side-effects**

- A sales lead is recorded as "New". If the visitor is signed in, the lead links to their account.
- It appears in the Control Panel Enquiries list. A Keydemand member follows up offline.
- No account change happens automatically.

---

###### Flow 6 — Becoming an Enterprise Brand (offline)

- **Actor:** The Keydemand team, then the brand.
- **Prerequisites:** An enquiry (Flow 5), a direct request, or sales outreach.
1. Keydemand and the brand agree terms offline. Requirements and brand parameters are collected outside the app.
2. A Keydemand admin creates or upgrades the account, sets up the brand page, sub-brands and saved **Formats** (size, frontage, floor, fit-out), adds each team member's mobile number, and assigns a Relationship Manager. Details: Control Panel guide.
3. Each team member signs in with their own number and code.
4. The brand sees: unlimited demands, the **Post for** sub-brand picker, a **Team demands** view, a Relationship Manager card, and locked-off WhatsApp and email.

**What changes for the brand**

| Area | Before | After |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 3 free | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 free | Unlimited |
| Demand form | Plain | Format picker. Asset class and constant fields can be pre-filled |
| Who can manage demands | The poster | **Every user of the brand** can read, edit, deactivate and delete all the brand's demands |
| Help | Contact page | Relationship Manager card, plus **Ask my RM** on each demand |
| WhatsApp and email | Optional | Off and locked |
| Deactivate or delete | Self-service | Only through Keydemand |

---

###### Flow 7 — Explore properties and projects

- **Actor:** A brand user, or a visitor.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Signed-in users see photos.
1. Open **Explore Properties** from the menu or bottom bar. The page opens on the saved city and the brand's own class.
2. Switch between **Property** and **Projects**. A **Demands** option does not appear.
3. Use filters. Sort by Most Recent, Price: Low to High, Price: High to Low, or Area: Largest First.
4. Turning on **Office** for the first time shows a notice that it is outside the brand's own category. The notice is asked once per visit.
5. Open a card for the full detail page.

**Filter groups**

| Group | Options |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing type | Property, Projects |
| Transaction | Lease, Sale |
| Asset class | Retail, F&B, Office (Managed Space is not offered) |
| Store type | Highstreet, Mall |
| Floor | Floor choices (ground, upper floors and bands) |
| Availability | Immediate, within 3, 6, 9 months |
| Fit-out | Furnished, unfurnished and similar |
| Amenities | The shared amenity list |
| Facilities | Washroom, parking, signage allowed |
| Legal | OC status |
| Ranges | Area and price ranges |
| Projects only | Project status, project type, Mixed Use, seats, total project size |

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand asks for a class it may not see | The request is narrowed silently to the allowed classes |
| Signed out | Photos hidden. Contact reveal asks the visitor to sign in first |
| Listing limited to certain audiences | Brand sees it only if one of the ticked groups describes it (for example Retail brand or Enterprise brand) |
| Cities | Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Pune and Hyderabad appear in the quick filters. The full served list is in the city picker |

---

###### Flow 8 — View a supplier's phone number (contact reveal)

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The listing is live and visible to the brand.
1. On a property or demand card or detail page, tap **View number**.
2. If signed out, the user is sent to sign in, then returned and the reveal continues.
3. The system checks, in order: already revealed (free, shown again), own listing, listing still live, audience allows the brand, then the allowance.
4. **Property or ordinary demand:** the number reveals at once in a **Contact Unlocked** pop-up with the contact's name, the number, a **Copy** button and a **Call [first name]** button.
5. A free reveal is counted.
6. After five free reveals the prompt appears: "Brand accounts include 5 free contact views. Go Enterprise to reveal unlimited supplier numbers, with priority matching and a dedicated relationship manager."

**System side-effects**

- A record of the reveal is saved with its source (free, subscription, owner, approved or Keydemand).
- The owner is told someone viewed their number, as an in-app "Someone viewed your contact" row and a line in the 6 pm summary.
- An enterprise brand is never counted.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing deactivated, deleted or not approved | "This listing is no longer available." |
| Own listing | "This is your own listing." |
| Listing hidden from the brand's group | "Property not found" |
| Free views used | The Enterprise prompt (individual) |
| Request closed because the listing ended | The free reveal is **given back** |

---

###### Flow 9 — Request hidden photos

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The owner marked some photos hidden.
1. On the property page, hidden photos show a **Request images** button.
2. A confirmation pop-up says **Image Request Sent** with "Awaiting owner approval". Button: **Got it**.
3. The owner is alerted (in-app, push, WhatsApp) with **Share images**.
4. **Approved:** the brand gets "Images are now available for [ID]" and sees all photos from then on.
5. **Declined:** "Your image request for [ID] was not approved." The request is closed.
6. No answer in 72 hours: the request expires.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| A second request for the same listing | "You have already sent a request for this listing." |
| Own listing | "You cannot send a request on your own listing." |
| Listing ended first | The request closes and the brand is told "Your request was closed because the property is no longer available." |

---

###### Flow 10 — Brand as recipient: approve or decline a contact request

- **Actor:** Brand user (any user of the brand for enterprise).
- **Prerequisites:** An agent or Keydemand member asked for the number on the brand's demand.

**Why this exists:** A demand posted by a brand is the one case where reveal needs approval. Every other number reveals at once.

1. The requester taps **View number** on the brand's demand. A request is created instead of a reveal. They see "Request sent — the owner will approve. Track it under Enquiries."
2. The brand is alerted (in-app, push, WhatsApp; individual brands only) with **Approve or decline**.
3. Open **Dashboard → Leads → Contact requests**. Each row shows the requester type, the demand and a **New** badge.
4. Press **Accept**: "Request approved — your number is now visible to them."
5. Or press **Reject**, confirm "Reject this request?", then "Request rejected".
6. The requester is told the result. Approved: "Contact request approved, tap to view the number." Declined: "Contact request not approved."
7. If the brand does nothing for **72 hours**, the request expires. The requester sees it as unanswered.

**System side-effects**

- Accepting writes the reveal record. The requester can now see the brand contact.
- A request already answered cannot be changed: "This request has already been actioned."
- If the demand ends before an answer, the row shows an "unavailable" label without Accept or Reject.

**Keydemand-held brand demands**

When Keydemand posts a demand on a brand's behalf, the demand **reads as the brand**. Nobody asks the brand to approve. The revealed phone is the Keydemand member's, shown under the brand's name (or "Retail brand" or "F&B brand" if the brand hides its name). Every active user of the brand is told of each reveal and enquiry, and the acting person is never told about their own action.

---

###### Flow 11 — Leads and "numbers viewed"

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. Open **Dashboard → Leads**.
2. **Contact requests** lists people asking for the brand's number, with the open ones flagged.
3. **Phone numbers viewed** lists people who unlocked the brand's number. Tapping a person shows their history.
4. The Leads card on the Overview shows an alert when a contact request is waiting.

Brands do **not** see an Image requests inbox, because brands do not post properties.

---

###### Flow 12 — Dashboard

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Brands see four tabs: **Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries**. There is no Properties tab.

| Tab | What it shows |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Overview** | Counts for Demands, Leads and Enquiries. Each opens its own tab. A short list of relevant properties and projects |
| **Demands** | The brand's demand cards, filterable by asset class. Each card shows matched properties and projects, a red dot for new matches and the status. Enterprise brands get **My demands / Team demands** |
| **Leads** | Contact requests received and numbers viewed (Flow 11) |
| **Enquiries** | What the brand sent: Numbers you've viewed, Contacts requested (with Pending, Accepted, Rejected), Images requested, Projects enquired |

Drafts appear here as "Unfinished listings — pick up where you left off", with Resume and Discard.

- A deactivated account shows an amber banner. A self-deactivated brand sees a reactivate option. A brand deactivated by Keydemand sees "Your account has been deactivated by Keydemand".

---

###### Flow 13 — Manage a demand (open, edit, deactivate, reactivate, delete)

- **Actor:** The poster, or any user of an enterprise brand.
- **Prerequisites:** The demand exists.
1. Open the demand from the dashboard. The owner bar offers **Edit**, **Deactivate** (or **Activate**), **Delete**, **Download as PDF** and **Copy link**. Enterprise brands also see **Ask my RM**.
2. **Edit:** the same form opens with stored values. After the first enquiry arrives, **four fields lock**: asset class, transaction type, city and location. Everything else stays editable. Locked fields rejected on save are reported by name.
3. **Deactivate:** a confirmation pop-up. The demand leaves matching. Open requests on it close. Its high-value lead, if any, is withdrawn. A receipt appears.
4. **Activate:** "Demand activated". A demand still waiting for approval cannot be switched on: "This demand is waiting for Keydemand approval and cannot be switched on yet."
5. **Delete:** a confirmation pop-up. "Demand deleted". Open requests close. The free slot is **not** given back.
6. **Fulfilled:** the system supports marking a demand fulfilled, which closes requests and withdraws the lead. The web app does not show a Fulfilled button on the demand page.

**Rules**

- Demands do not expire under the current matching rules.
- An unauthorised person who opens an edit link is sent back to the demand page.
- A Keydemand member can edit only on accounts whose team they are on. Other edits happen in the Control Panel.

---

###### Flow 14 — Demand audience ("Who can see this")

- A Brand's demand is visible to **agents and the Keydemand team**. The Brand has no control.
- An agent cannot reveal or enquire on a brand demand unless agents are in its audience.
- A demand routed as high-value (Flow 15) drops agents until Keydemand releases it.
- A release adds agents back only if the poster's stored choice included them. If not, the release is refused: "Agents not chosen".
- Agents who see a brand's demand through matching see it as a **verified requirement**. They never browse the brand's demand list.

---

###### Flow 15 — High-value and Keydemand-managed routing

- **Actor:** The system; then the Keydemand team.
- **Prerequisites:** A live brand demand.
1. After posting, the system checks the demand against the **High Value Lead rules**: the city must be one of eight major cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi), the asset class and transaction type must match a rule, and the demand size must reach the rule's minimum.
2. If it qualifies, the demand is **hidden from agents** and a **High Value Lead** is opened and assigned to Keydemand members. They are told "A demand in [city] now qualifies as high-value and has been assigned to you."
3. **What the brand sees:** nothing special. The demand looks normal in its own dashboard. Nobody tells the brand the word "high-value".
4. Keydemand contacts the brand directly.
5. If the demand is edited or the rules change, the lead is re-checked. A demand that stops qualifying is released and its lead is **Withdrawn**.
6. Ending the demand (delete, deactivate, fulfil) withdraws the lead in every state.

**Rules**

- Demands posted by agents are exempt.
- Managed Space demands are handled differently and are not part of this check.
- When Keydemand later releases the lead, only subscribed agents with a matching live property are told.

---

###### Flow 16 — How matching and the % Match score work

- **Actor:** The system.
- **Prerequisites:** A live, approved demand.

**What the brand sees:** Matched properties and projects appear on the demand card, in the dashboard, and in the 6 pm summary, each with a percentage.

**Step 1 — hidden or shown:** A listing is hidden if it is not live, the asset class does not go with the demand (Retail and F&B go together), the transaction differs, the city differs, it is more than 3 km from every requested location, the area is below 75% or above 125% of the request, or (Retail and F&B) the ceiling is more than 1 ft lower than asked.

**Step 2 — the percentage:** Each asset class has its own weights. A requirement the demand did not ask for counts in full. A requirement the demand asked for that the property leaves blank earns nothing.

| Row | Retail weight | F&B weight |
| :---- | :---: | :---: |
| Location | 20 | 18.75 |
| Area | 20 | 18.75 |
| Ceiling height | 20 | 18.75 |
| Floor | 20 | 18.75 |
| Fit-outs | 5 | 5 |
| Possession | 5 | 5 |
| Frontage | 5 | 5 |
| Store type | 5 | 0 |
| Cooking type | — | 5 |
| Non-veg | — | 5 |

**Step 3:** Matches below **50%** are left out of lists, counts and the digest. Results are sorted best first. Ties go to the nearer listing, then the most recently updated.

**Not scored:** price (even if the demand has a budget), washroom, parking, mezzanine, OC, lease terms, building age.

**Other rules**

- Projects are matched on class, transaction, city, unit size range (10% below the smallest to 20% above the largest) and the 3 km rule.
- The brand's own listings may match (not applicable to brands, who post no properties).
- A new match is highlighted until the brand opens it.

---

###### Flow 17 — Projects and "Show Interest"

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in to submit interest in one tap.
1. Open a project from Explore (Projects), a rail, or a demand's relevant projects.
2. Press **Show Interest**. The profile details are sent automatically. A pop-up says "Thank you for showing interest." The button then reads as already sent.
3. A signed-out visitor sees a short enquiry form instead.
4. The interest goes to the project's Keydemand Relationship Manager. The developer's contact is not revealed.
5. **Dashboard → Enquiries → Projects enquired** lists every project the brand reached out to.
6. A project can also be downloaded as a PDF when signed in. Signed out: "Sign in to download this project as a PDF".

---

###### Flow 18 — Saved (favourites)

1. Tap the heart on a property or project card. Signed out, the visitor is asked to sign in first and the save then completes.
2. **Saved** has two tabs for a Brand: Properties and Projects. The Demands tab does not appear.
3. Each tab shows the count and the same cards as search.

---

###### Flow 19 — Notifications centre and preferences

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. The bell shows an unread count. **Notifications** has **All** and **Unread** tabs and **Mark all read**.
2. Each row has a call-to-action button that opens the related page.
3. **Profile → Notifications** has switches for **Email**, **WhatsApp** and (mobile app only) **Push**.
4. Email shows only when the account has an email address.
5. **Enterprise brands:** Email and WhatsApp are off and locked, with the line "Off for enterprise accounts — your Keydemand team contacts you directly". Only in-app and push continue.
6. Only promotional messages can be switched off. Messages about requests, relevance and leads are always sent.
7. The 6 pm India-time summary is one roll-up of new matches and other digest items. It is skipped when there is nothing to report.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Push blocked on the phone | "Blocked on this device — enable Notifications for Keydemand in your device settings" |
| Push turn-off | "Push notifications turned off on this device" |
| WhatsApp switch fails | "Could not update WhatsApp preference" |

---

###### Flow 20 — View and edit the profile

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. **Profile** shows Personal Details (name, mobile, official email, designation) and Business Details (company name, experience), plus Preferences (asset class and city).
2. **Edit Profile** allows: name, email, photo, designation, cities, brand description, company name, experience, and notification choices.
3. The **mobile number cannot be changed**. The asset class is locked to the brand's own.
4. Email is required and must be valid. Errors: "Email is required for this account" and "Email is not a valid address".
5. Saving asks "Save these changes?". Cancelling with edits asks "Discard your changes?".
6. A **Verified** badge shows beside the name. Enterprise brands also show an **Enterprise** badge.

---

###### Flow 21 — Deactivate and reactivate the account

- **Actor:** An individual brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Individual account.
1. **Profile → More → Deactivate account**. A pop-up asks "Deactivate account?".
2. On confirm: the user's listings are hidden, their demands are taken down, and they stop showing as active.
3. On the next sign-in a pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now**. A **Reactivate account** button also sits on the Profile page.
4. Reactivating restores only what this deactivation hid. Demands a Keydemand member or the system hid separately stay hidden.
5. Deactivated by Keydemand: the user cannot reactivate. The message says "Your account was deactivated by Keydemand. Please contact support."

**Enterprise accounts:** The server refuses: "Enterprise and Keydemand-team accounts are managed by the Keydemand team — please contact your relationship manager." The Profile page can still show the button to an enterprise brand (see Section 7).

---

###### Flow 22 — Request account deletion

- **Actor:** An individual brand user.
1. **Profile → More → Delete Account**. A pop-up shows Full Name, Phone and Email read-only, an optional **Reason for leaving** list, and a tick to confirm.
2. Submit. The account is **queued for review**, not wiped on the spot. The words on screen say "request" for that reason.
3. The Delete Account page explains what is **Removed**, what is **Taken offline** and what is **Retained where required**.
4. The user can withdraw the request: "Cancel your deletion request?" then "Deletion request withdrawn".
5. Keydemand processes it from the Control Panel's Account Deletions list.

**Edge cases:** Enterprise accounts are refused. A second request while one is pending returns the first request's date. A request already processed cannot be withdrawn: "Your deletion request has already been processed."

---

###### Flow 23 — Help, Relationship Manager and assistance

- **Actor:** An enterprise brand user, or any brand.
1. **Help for everyone:** the Contact page lists the support email and phone, and the FAQs page answers common questions (hidden in the iPhone app).
2. **Relationship Manager card (enterprise):** name, designation, a **Call** button (phone number) and an **Email** button. Reach it from the profile menu entry **Relationship Manager**.
3. If no manager is assigned yet: "Your relationship manager will be assigned shortly", with the support email.
4. **Ask my RM** (enterprise brands, on a demand or on the card): choose **Edit, Deactivate, Delete, Activate or Other**. A note is optional, but **required for Other**: "Tell your RM what you need help with."
5. Sent: "Request sent — your Relationship Manager has been notified."
6. A second request for the same action on the same demand: "You already asked your RM about this — it is still open."
7. **Individual brands:** "Relationship Manager help is available to enterprise brands. Contact Keydemand to upgrade."

**System side-effects**

- The account's Keydemand team and the assigned manager are alerted. The manager gets in-app, email and WhatsApp.
- If no manager is assigned, an email goes to the operations inbox.
- Keydemand resolves the request in the Control Panel and the brand is told.

---

###### Flow 24 — Sign out

1. Use **Logout** from the profile menu.
2. The session ends on the device. Saved city and draft choices stay on the device.

###### 5. Limits and Rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free demands (individual) | 3 per brand, lifetime |
| Free contact reveals (individual) | 5 per user, lifetime |
| Enterprise | Unlimited demands and reveals |
| One-time code | 6 digits |
| Enquiry and contact-request expiry | 72 hours |
| Hidden-photo request expiry | 72 hours |
| Fields locked after first enquiry response | Asset class, transaction type, city, location |
| Demand expiry | None under current rules |
| Match minimum | 50% |
| Match distance | 3 km from a requested location |
| Match area window | 75% to 125% of the request |
| Other nearby localities | Up to 3 |
| Digest time | 6 pm India time |
| High-value cities | Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi |
| Demand audience | Agents and Keydemand (fixed) |
| Brand explore scope | Retail, F&B, Office |
| Brand post scope | Own asset class only |
| Email for sign-up | Required, format and mail-server checked |
| Account deactivate or delete | Individual only |
