###### 1\. Purpose and Who Uses It

**The Control Panel is Keydemand's internal operations console.** It is where staff create customer accounts, approve listings, route large leads, sell and adjust subscriptions, and watch the health of the platform. End customers never see it.

###### What It Is For

| Job | Where It Happens |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Onboard customers** who cannot self-register (developers, operators, enterprise brands and tenants) | User Management, Enterprise |
| **Run quality control** on new listings | Listing Management, Bulk Upload |
| **Post on behalf of customers** (properties, demands, projects, centres) | Listing Management |
| **Route high-value demands** to the Keydemand team | High Value Leads |
| **Handle inbound sales interest** and account deletion requests | Enquiries |
| **Sell and adjust subscriptions** | Subscription Management, agent pages |
| **Control who can sign up** by email domain | Email Domains |
| **Manage staff access** | Control Panel Users |
| **Watch the business and the system** | Dashboard, App Insights, Observability |
| **Finish migrated v1 data** | V1 Completion Queue |

###### Who Uses It

| Operator Type | Typical Person | What They Mostly Do |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Super Admin** | Tech lead, business head (two people in every environment) | Everything, including staff security and system settings |
| **Admin** | Operations manager | Customer, listing, subscription and lead operations; can manage staff except super admins |
| **Contributor** | Data-entry or content staff | Create and edit listings and projects, bulk upload, view users |
| **Business Viewer** | Leadership, finance | Dashboard and Business Insights, with export |
| **Tech Viewer** | Engineers, support | Technical Insights, with export |
| **Custom roles** | Anyone | Any mix of permissions a super admin or admin builds |

> **Two separate identities.** Control Panel operators sign in with an email and password. They are not customers and share no sign-in with the customer app. Keydemand team members who use the customer app (relationship managers and others) are managed from this panel but sign in there with phone and code.

---

###### 2\. Access Model

###### 2.1 Sign-In and Session Security

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Credentials** | Email and password. There is no self-registration. A super admin or admin creates the account. |
| **First sign-in** | New and reset accounts receive a one-time password by email. The first sign-in forces a password change, and there is no way to skip it. |
| **Password rules** | At least 6 characters, with one uppercase letter, one number and one special character. The form lists what is missing. |
| **Two-factor code** | When switched on for the environment, a 6-digit code is emailed after the password. It lasts 5 minutes and works once. **On in production.** |
| **Code limits** | 5 wrong codes void the code. Resend is allowed after 60 seconds, up to 3 times. At most 5 codes are issued per person in 15 minutes. |
| **Code delivery failure** | The sign-in fails with a "try again" message. The system never lets someone in because email failed. |
| **Password lockout** | 5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes. It unlocks by itself, and a correct sign-in resets the count. |
| **Forgot password** | A 6-digit code is emailed (15 minutes). **Switched off in production**, where a super admin resets credentials instead. |
| **Session length** | Access lasts 30 minutes and renews quietly. A session left idle for 24 hours signs out. One in use stays signed in. |
| **Sign out** | Signs out this device. "Sign out everywhere" ends every session for the person. |
| **Instant revocation** | Disabling a person, changing their password, or changing their role or permissions takes effect on their next click. |
| **Stolen-session protection** | Reusing an old session token signs the person out everywhere and is logged. |
| **Security alert emails** | Sent to the person and to the DevOps group (UAT and production) for: sign-in from a new device or location, any super admin sign-in, 5 wrong passwords or codes, password changes and resets, and role or permission changes. |

###### 2.2 Operator Roles

| Role | What It Means | Who Can Change It |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Super Admin** | Every permission. Fixed set that cannot be edited. | Cannot be edited by anyone |
| **Admin** | Every permission except the two reserved for super admins (system settings and site-down). | Super admin only |
| **Contributor** | Create and edit listings and projects, bulk upload, formats, view users and dashboard. Cannot approve bulk uploads. | Super admin only |
| **Business Viewer** | Dashboard, Business Insights, export. Built in. | Super admin only |
| **Tech Viewer** | Technical Insights, export. Built in. Cannot change log levels. | Super admin only |
| **Custom** | Any selection of permissions. Built from the Control Panel Users screen. | Admin or super admin, within limits below |

###### 2.3 Staff Protection Rules

| Rule | Effect |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Only a super admin** may create a super admin, move anyone into or out of that role, disable or reset a super admin, or edit a built-in role | An admin who tries is refused, and the refusal is logged |
| **At most 2 active super admins** | A third cannot be created, promoted or re-enabled. Today the two are fixed in every environment. |
| **The last active super admin** cannot be disabled, deleted or demoted | Protects against lockout |
| **No self-escalation** | A non-super admin cannot give a role a permission they do not hold themselves |
| **Only a super admin can delete** an operator account | Admins can disable but not delete |
| **You cannot disable or delete yourself** | Prevents accidental lockout |
| **An operator holding a parked Keydemand hand-over cannot be deleted** | The work must be completed first |

###### 2.6 Keydemand Team Members (Customer-App Staff)

Keydemand team members are customer-app users that this panel manages. They are not Control Panel operators.

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Sub-roles** | Keydemand Agent and Business Relationship Manager (BRM). The BRM adds broker management. |
| **Role templates** | Each sub-role has a default set of customer-app permissions, editable on the Keydemand Team "Roles" screen. Changing a template changes everyone who follows it. |
| **Per-person overrides** | A member can carry their own permission set that replaces the template. "Reset to template" removes it. |
| **Always on** | Dashboard and Explore Property cannot be removed. |
| **The 14 toggles** | Dashboard, Explore Property, Explore Demand, Post Property, Post Demand, Broker Management, My Listings, KD Listings, Assigned Brands, KD Brands, Tagged Projects, All Projects, High Value Leads, Notifications and Enquiries. |
| **Enforced toggles** | Post Property, Post Demand and Explore Demand are actually enforced on the server. The others control what the app shows. |
| **Account teams** | Enterprise brands and tenants have a Point of Contact (POC) plus an optional Keydemand team. "RM", "Account Handler" and "POC" are the same role. |
| **Hand-over** | A member cannot be deactivated or deleted while they still hold accounts, listings, assignments or pending enquiries. The work is moved to another member, or parked with a Control Panel admin. See Flow 13 in the flows document. |

###### 4\. Module-by-Module Product Documentation

###### 4.1 Sign-In, Password and Session

**Purpose:** Let staff in safely, and stop others.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Email and password sign-in | Identify the operator | Email, password | Signed in, or code step if two-factor is on |
| Emailed sign-in code | Second factor in production | 6-digit code | Signed in. Wrong, expired and locked states show clear messages. |
| Resend code | Recover from a lost email | Resend button | New code after a 60-second wait, up to 3 times |
| Forced password change | Retire the emailed one-time password | First sign-in or after a reset | Cannot enter the console until a valid new password is set |
| Forgot password | Self-service recovery | Email, then emailed code and new password | All sessions end. **Off in production.** |
| Sign out and sign out everywhere | End sessions | Menu | Immediate revocation |
| Silent renewal | Avoid mid-task logouts | Automatic | Session extends while in use. 24-hour idle limit. |

**Validations and errors:** wrong credentials, disabled account, locked account (15 minutes), too many codes, expired code, weak password, email delivery failure, reset switched off.

###### 4.2 Dashboard

**Purpose:** A fast daily read on the business.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary outcomes** | Headline daily numbers | Open the page, choose Today, 7 days or 30 days | High-value leads, enterprise enquiries (split by persona), project leads and Keydemand team, each as "new in window" and "total" |
| **Secondary outcomes** | Deeper numbers | Expand the section | Subscriptions (active and expired), users by role, demands, properties and projects by asset class and poster type, leads, marketing enquiries, deleted properties, account deletions |
| **Per-member block** | Check one team member's work | Pick a Keydemand member | Enterprise accounts, high-value leads assigned, listings uploaded, projects assigned, leads |
| **Account and listing detail** | Register-level counts | Expand the detail block | Agents, tenants, developers and operators, Keydemand, enquiries and listings, with asset-class donuts |
| **Sidebar badges** | Show register sizes | Automatic | Counts beside the four account registers and Enterprise |

"Today" starts at midnight India time. The same numbers feed the daily admin email, so the screen and the email never disagree.

> **Indian mobile numbers on every create *(added, from 2026-10-30)*.** Customers sign in by SMS code, and codes go only to Indian mobiles (+91 followed by 10 digits starting 6 to 9). So that no account is created that can never sign in, the Control Panel applies the same rule when staff create an account, **before** the duplicate-phone check. It applies to: create Keydemand team member (replacing the looser international check), create agent, create tenant or occupier, add a member to a tenant account, create enterprise brand (primary user and each additional user), and add a user to an enterprise brand. Staff see "Enter a valid Indian mobile number (+91 followed by 10 digits starting 6-9)" with the field named. The form's phone box already adds +91, so only a number starting 0 to 5 is newly refused. Editing an existing account and bulk upload are unaffected. The allowed country codes are an environment setting (default India only).

###### Demands Keydemand holds for a brand *(added 2026-11-05)*

A **Keydemand-held brand demand** is a demand filed under a brand but posted by Keydemand: every migrated v1 brand demand, demands posted from the Control Panel on a brand's behalf (4.11), and Format-mode bulk uploads for brands.

**What changed (2026-11-03):** before, an agent who tapped "View number" saw the Keydemand member's own phone at once, and no lead was recorded. Now the tap sends a **contact request**, and no number is shown until someone answers it.

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Who can answer** | The poster, the brand's users, or the brand's Keydemand team (POC and team members). Any Keydemand member can also answer. The first answer wins; a second is refused. |
| **What is shared** | The accepter's contact. If the brand hides its name, a brand user is shared as phone only, under "Retail brand" or "F&B brand". |
| **Brand's own side** | The brand's users and its Keydemand team tapping the button on the brand's own demand get no request and no charge. |
| **Keydemand demand with no brand** | Unchanged. Immediate reveal. |
| **If nobody answers** | Reminder at 48 hours. The request expires at 72 hours and the viewer's free contact view is returned. |
| **Where it appears** | As a lead on the demand's Leads tab (4.10) and under Listing Leads (4.14). The Received tab now also lists requests addressed to the responders above, not only to the recipient. |
| **Back-fill (migration 129)** | Each earlier phone view on such a demand is recorded as an accepted contact-request lead, so lead history is complete. The viewer keeps the number they had and nothing is sent. Left out: views by Keydemand staff, the poster's own view, deleted viewers, deleted demands, and views that already have a request. The demand's lead total is unchanged. |

###### 4.11 Posting on Behalf and Bulk Upload

**Purpose:** Put supply and demand on the platform faster and with the same rules as the customer app.

| **Post a demand for a customer** | Create demand | Shared post form | Goes live at once, then checked for high-value routing. The customer is notified. |
| **Post a brand's demand as Keydemand** | Brands with no users of their own | Choose the brand | Demand is filed under the brand and flagged Keydemand-managed. The brand's users are notified. |
| **Poster checks** | Same identity rules as the app | Automatic | Poster must be live. An occupier posts managed space only. A brand posts its own class only. Developers and operators cannot post demands. |
| **Agent subscription check** | Treat agents fairly | Automatic when the switch is on | Covered city and class, or the one free listing |
| **Bulk upload** | Load many listings | Upload a sheet | See Flow 22\. Sheets of demands (including enterprise Format mode), properties, developer projects and centres. Up to 5 MB, 2,000 rows and 120 columns. |
| **Templates and samples** | Avoid mistakes | Download | Blank template per variant and 18 worked samples, with instructions and common mistakes |
| **Validation report** | Fix before anything is created | Upload result | Row-by-row issues with cell reference, message and hint. Downloadable error report. |
| **Create for review, approve, reject** | Two-person control | Commit, then review | Rows are hidden until a reviewer approves them |

###### 4.13 High Value Leads (HVL)

**Purpose:** Keep large demands with Keydemand until it chooses to release them.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Rules** | Define "high value" | City (Tier-1 only), asset class (retail, F\&B, office), minimum size, optional maximum, transaction type, assignees | New and edited rules re-check every live demand in that market. Managed space is not an HVL class. |
| **City switch** | Turn a city on or off | Toggle | Re-checks retail, F\&B and office rules in that city together |
| **Lead register** | Work the queue | Open the page | Filters: status, city, asset class, assignee, search by lead ID or locality. Withdrawn leads are hidden unless asked. |
| **Assign** | Choose who works a lead | Assign dialog | Manual assignment wins over rule changes |
| **Release to agents (unlock)** | Open the demand to agents | Unlock | Only if the poster allowed agents. Refused otherwise. Subscribed, covered agents with a matching live property are notified. |
| **Take back (relock)** | Undo a release | Relock | Removes agent visibility only if the release added it. Already-sent notices and taken contacts cannot be undone. |
| **Delete a rule** | Retire a rule | Delete | Leads it created are re-checked and may be withdrawn |
| **Automatic upkeep** | Keep the register honest | Automatic | Leads follow approval, edits, rule changes and city switches. Ending a demand always withdraws its lead. |

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Marketing Enquiries** | Inbound sales and onboarding interest | Open the page | Types: developer, operator, enterprise, project interest, landing page, managed-office interest. Filters: type, status, city, assignee, search, sort. |
| **Assign a lead** | Give it an owner | Pick an active Keydemand member | The member gets an in-app notice. Unassign is allowed. |
| **Change status** | Track progress | New, Contacted, Closed or Converted | "Converted" needs the customer's live account of the right role |
| **Repeat submissions** | Avoid duplicates | Automatic | A repeat from the same phone and role updates the open lead and counts submissions |
| **Listing Leads** | See platform-wide interest in listings | Open the page | Enquiries, contact and image requests. Filters: status, type, city, raised by, owner, dates, search. Each row names its listing. |
| **Account Deletions** | Process deletion requests | Open the page | Tabs by status with counts. Detail shows active listings, active subscription and history. |
| **Process, decline or log an emailed request** | Close the loop | Buttons on the detail | Process deletes the account like the normal delete, ends the subscription (no automatic refund) and signs the person out. Decline needs a note the user can see. |

###### 4.15 Control Panel Users and Email Domains

**Purpose:** Manage who can use the panel, and who can sign up to the app.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Staff list** | See operators | Open the page | Filters: search, active status, role. Shows "pending sign-in" for accounts that never signed in. |
| **Create operator** | Add staff | Name, email, optional phone and city, role | One-time password emailed. Disposable or undeliverable emails are refused. |
| **Edit operator** | Change role and details | Edit | Role changes email the operator and are logged |
| **Disable or enable** | Pause access | Status action | Disabling ends every session at once |
| **Reset credentials** | Recover or rotate | Reset | New one-time password, sessions end, a security alert is sent |
| **Delete operator** | Remove | Delete (super admin only) | Soft delete, sessions end |
| **Roles** | Define permission sets | Create or edit a custom role | Permissions grouped by module. Built-in roles are read-only to non-super admins. |
| **Email Domains** | Block or allow domains | Add or remove rules | Adds to the built-in disposable-domain list or carves exceptions. Takes effect within about a minute. Protected domains (major mail providers and Keydemand's own) cannot be blocked. A lookup shows how many accounts already use a domain. |

###### 4.16 V1 Migration Screens

**Purpose:** Help staff finish data brought over from the old platform.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Completion queue — properties** | Find migrated listings the edit form would refuse | Open the tab | Lists each record with the missing fields, plus counts by field. Filters: city, asset class, search. |
| **Completion queue — profiles** | Find migrated agents with missing profile data | Open the tab | Missing asset class, cities, email or a valid RERA number |
| **Migration notes** | See what was changed during migration | Notes panel on a migrated record | Read-only notes. Not shown for records created in v2. |
| **v1 numbers** | Keep old references useful | Search and ID cell | v1 numbers are searchable and shown. They cannot be edited. |

A record leaves the queue on its own once it is saved complete. Fixing happens on the ordinary edit screens.

###### 4.17 App Insights

**Purpose:** Read-only business and technical analytics, built from the live database and AWS monitoring.

| Section | Views |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Business** | Overview (daily pulse, biggest movers) · Users and Growth · **Acquisition and Sign-ups** *(added)* · Revenue and Subscriptions · Marketplace · Engagement and Leads · Cities and Regions · KD Team and Operations · Live |
| **Technical** | Health · API Performance · Errors · Dependencies · Jobs and Pipelines · Auth and Security · Payments Pipeline · Messaging · Clients · Runtime Config |

&nbsp;

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **KPI strip with change vs previous period** | Quick read | Open a view | Headline numbers with a comparison to the previous period |
| **Collapsible cards** | Load only what is needed | Expand a card | Trends, funnels, retention cohorts, breakdowns |
| **Filters (Business)** | Slice the data | Dates, day/week/month, compare, cities, regions, asset class, role, exclude internal accounts, include v1 | Applied where the view supports it. Filters a view ignores are listed. |
| **Filters (Technical)** | Choose a window | 1 hour, 6 hours, 24 hours, 7 days or custom (max 7 days); service | Charts and tables for that window |
| **Live view** | See who is online now | Open Live | Online now, signed in versus not, active in 30 and 60 minutes, by platform, role and city, screens in use. Refreshed on request. |
| **Help on every widget** | Explain each number | "?" icon | What it is, how it is built, its source, caveats |
| **Export** | Share or analyse | CSV or Excel button | Whole view, same filters. Logged with the operator and row count. |
| **Refresh** | Get fresh data | Refresh icon | Skips the 5-minute cache (30 seconds on Live) |
| **Privacy** | Protect customers | Automatic | Aggregates only. Groups under 5 people show as "under 5". Team members are labelled by a short code, not by name. |
| **Time limit (Technical)** | Keep pages responsive | Automatic | Widgets still running after 45 seconds show "unavailable". The rest still renders. |
| **Daily snapshots** | History for active-user trends | Automatic, 00:15 India time | A daily platform row and one per city, used for daily, weekly and monthly active users and paying agents |
| **Presence** | Live online counts | Automatic | Every signed-in customer action stamps their last activity (at most every 15 minutes). Can be switched off. |
| **Internal accounts excluded** | Honest numbers | Default on | Staff, seed and test accounts are left out |

###### 4.18 Observability (Super Admin)

**Purpose:** Let super admins turn up logging for troubleshooting without a deploy.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Log levels per service** | Raise or lower detail | Choose service and level, give a reason | Applies within about 30 seconds. Every change is logged. |
| **Debug and trace expiry** | Prevent leaving debug on | Required expiry, 240 minutes at most | Reverts automatically. Cannot apply to the default level. |
| **Debug for specific users** | Trace one customer's problem | Target users, up to a limit | Detailed logs only for them |
| **Clear overrides** | Return to normal | Clear action | Back to the default |
| **Error digest settings** | Daily error email | Switch on or off, recipients, send even when clean, reason | Controls the 08:30 India time email |

###### Acquisition & Sign-ups view *(added 2026-11-05)*

**Purpose:** Answer "where do visitors come from, how far do they get through sign-up, and where do they drop off". Read-only, same permission as the other Business views (App Insights, view Business), with the same CSV and Excel export.

| Part | What It Shows |
| :---- | :---- |
| **KPI strip** | Visitors landed, sign-ups opened, visit-to-sign-up rate, accounts registered, accounts registered from a campaign. No comparison with the previous period. |
| **Funnels** | Overall sign-up funnel: landed, opened sign-up, picked a role, code sent, code verified, saw the form, registered. Plus one funnel per persona, from the role screen on. Sign-ins of existing accounts are left out. |
| **Sources** | Where visitors arrive from: campaign tags (source, medium, campaign, content), referring websites, and Facebook / Instagram in-app browsers versus everything else. |
| **Drop-off** | Refusals people hit while signing up or in, by step, error code and the first field the error named. Counts requests, not people, so a retry counts again. |
| **Campaigns** | New accounts by the campaign source, campaign name and platform (website, Android, iOS) of their first visit, and campaign sign-ups by persona. |

- **Range limit:** the web-traffic parts (funnels, sources, drop-off) cover 7 days at most.
- **Privacy:** counts are distinct visitors; cells under 5 show as "<5".
- **Visit-to-sign-up is approximate**, because visitors come from web signals and accounts from the database.
- **Campaign and platform columns** fill only for accounts created after sign-up attribution was switched on. Older accounts show "not recorded" or "(none)".
- **Data source:** first-party web signals sent by the website and app, the API access logs, and the user records. Not Google Analytics.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **First-party web signals** | Feed the Acquisition view without a third-party tool | The website and app send usage events to the platform | Events are logged and counted. Crawlers are ignored; over-limit or malformed events are dropped quietly. |
| **Sign-up attribution** | Know which campaign created an account | Saved at sign-up: first-touch campaign tags, platform, trigger | Stored on the new user and on marketing leads, only while the switch is on |
| **Two runtime switches** | Turn collection off without a deploy | Ops changes a setting in AWS Parameter Store | Takes effect within about 30 seconds. No Control Panel screen changes them. |

> **Operational additions *(added 2026-11-01)*:**
> - **Scheduled jobs are easier to diagnose.** A crashed job now writes a failure record. Jobs that carry on past failing items (daily digest, admin newsletter, incomplete-registration notices) are flagged "partial", and a new alarm, `scheduled-job-partial`, emails on production at one or more a day. Nothing about what the jobs do changed.
> - **Browser-error reports are clearer.** They name the endpoint with ids hidden and the error class, include the error page's reference, and no longer count a cancelled request as a network failure. This covers the Control Panel too.
> - **Privacy in provider logs.** Phone and email are masked in SMS, WhatsApp and email provider log lines.

###### 5\. Notifications and Emails the Panel Sends

###### 5.1 Emails to Operators (internal mail)

Subjects carry an environment label (for example "\[PROD\]") and replies go to the monitored contact inbox. These are never held back by the non-production recipient allow-list.

| Email | Trigger | Recipient |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **One-time password** | Operator created, or credentials reset | The operator |
| **Sign-in code** | Two-factor sign-in | The operator |
| **Password reset code** | Forgot password (off in production) | The operator |
| **Security alerts** | New device, super admin sign-in, repeated failures, password change, credential reset, role or permission change | The operator, plus the DevOps group on UAT and production |
| **Role change notice** | Role assignment changed | The operator |
| **Daily admin newsletter** | Every day at 08:00 India time | Every active super admin and admin |
| **Daily error digest** | Every day at 08:30 India time | Configured recipients (the "Daily New" newsletter and the digest are separate emails) |

> **Where technical and ops mail goes *(added, interim until the Google groups accept outside senders)*:** technical mail (alarms, error digest, security alert copy, deploy mail) goes to `tech@keydemand.in` on UAT and PROD since 2026-11-01. PROD also keeps the DevOps group as a second alarm and budget recipient. DEV and SIT send none. Business ops mail goes to `ops@keydemand.in` on PROD, `himanshu@keydemand.in` on UAT and `john.a@futuristglobal.com` on DEV and SIT (since 2026-10-31). Wherever this document says "DevOps group", read `tech@keydemand.in` for UAT and PROD.

###### 5.2 Notifications to Customers and Staff Triggered by Panel Actions

| Action | Who Is Notified | Through |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Listing posted on someone's behalf | The poster (property or demand posted notice) | Customer notification channels |
| Demand posted on a brand's behalf | The brand's active users | Customer notification channels |
| POC assigned to an account | The Keydemand member | In-app and other channels |
| Marketing lead assigned | The Keydemand member | In-app |
| High-value lead assigned, reassigned or withdrawn | The assigned Keydemand members | In-app. Several changes at once collapse into one summary. |
| High-value lead released | Subscribed, covered agents with a matching live property | In-app, linking to that property. Never worded "high-value". Never sent twice for the same lead. |
| Complimentary subscription granted | The agent | Same "subscription activated" notice as a purchase |
| Listing approved or rejected | The owner (per the lifecycle design; delivery not separately verified) | Customer notification channels |
| Agent requests contact on a Keydemand-held brand demand *(added)* | The brand's users and its Keydemand team | In-app and other customer channels |
| Contact request left unanswered *(added)* | Reminder at 48 h to the responders; "expired" notice to the requester at 72 h | Customer notification channels |

> **Messaging hold:** On DEV and SIT, email is held. Panel actions still succeed and the mail is only logged, so no sign-in code arrives there unless the address is on the allow-list.

###### 6\. Feature Switches and Environment Differences

| Setting | DEV | SIT | UAT | PROD | Effect on the Panel |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Two-factor sign-in** | Off unless switched on by ops | Same | Same | **On** | A code is emailed after the password. Ops can change it without a deploy. No screen changes it. |
| **Forgot-password self-service** | On | On | On | **Off** | In production a super admin resets credentials |
| **Listing auto-approval** | On | On | On | **Off** | Customer posts wait for moderation in production. Panel posts on behalf are always auto-approved. |
| **Old "legacy proxy" admin routes** | Available | Available | Available | **Off** | Production exposes only the Control Panel API |
| **Enforce agent subscription on panel posts** | Off by default | Off by default | Off by default | Set per environment | When on, a post or bulk row for an agent needs coverage or the one free listing |
| **Messaging hold** | Email, WhatsApp, SMS held | Same | Push only | Off | Held mail is logged, not sent |
| **Security alert copy to DevOps group** | Off | Off | On | On | Extra copy of every security alert |
| **Relevancy v4 "Weighted" scoring** | On | On | On | On | Used on every match panel in the panel |
| **API documentation page** | On | On | On | Off | Interactive docs only outside production |
| **Presence tracking** | On | On | On | On | Powers the Live view. Can be switched off. |
| **Session idle limit** | 24 hours | 24 hours | 24 hours | 24 hours | Same everywhere |
| **Web signals intake** *(added)* | Per-environment setting | Same | Same | Off unless set | When off, the Acquisition view's visitor and funnel numbers stay empty. Changed by ops in AWS Parameter Store, live within about 30 seconds. No Control Panel screen. |
| **Sign-up attribution** *(added)* | Per-environment setting | Same | Same | Off unless set | When off, new accounts carry no campaign or platform, so the Campaigns part stays empty. Same runtime switch mechanism. |

> **Two-factor on a fresh environment:** the other panel automation (regression harnesses) cannot sign in with two-factor on until they handle the code step.

> **Messaging hold update *(added)*:** on DEV and SIT, email to the business-ops address is now let through the hold (the only address that is). Push stays on in DEV, SIT and UAT through the non-production Firebase project.

| **Newsletter and digest recipients** | Newsletter goes to active super admins and admins. Error digest recipients come from settings or a fallback list. Exact production recipients were not checked. |
| **Business and Technical Insights part lists** | Taken from the guide. The code-side manifest is the source of truth at run time. |
| **Acquisition & Sign-ups view on production** *(added 2026-11-05)* | The view exists in code. Whether web signals and sign-up attribution are switched on in production was not checked; they default to off there. |
| **Brand-held demand contact-request wording** *(added 2026-11-05)* | Taken from the capability matrix and regression harness. Final notification copy was not reviewed. |
| **Changes after 2026-11-03** *(added 2026-11-05)* | Only changes with a dated note in the repo were captured. Undated edits may be missing. |

###### 9.3 Product Questions

1. **Should the Contributor be able to approve its own uploads?** Today it cannot, which enforces two-person control.  
2. **Should an Admin be able to see Technical Insights by default?** Today yes. The Tech Viewer role exists for engineers.  
3. **Should the assign-lead action on High Value Leads use the "unlock" permission?** Today it needs "manage rules", which means someone allowed to release leads may not be allowed to assign them.  
4. **Should email-domain rules and staff management share one permission?** Today both need "Control Panel Users — manage".  
5. **Should deleted HVL rules be restorable?** Today they are not.  
6. **Should demands posted by the panel also respect the agent subscription by default?** Today it is off unless an environment sets it.  
7. **Who receives the admin-team emails in 5.3?** Options are a shared inbox, every active super admin and admin (as with the daily newsletter), or a configurable list. It is also open whether bell alerts should follow role permissions, for example showing sign-up alerts only to operators with Users — view.  
8. **How should high-volume activity alerts be handled?** Contact viewed, images requested, contact requested and phone number viewed fire on every action and could flood the bell. Options are per-event, batched, or a separate filter on Recent Activity.  
9. **When do the daily summary emails go out?** New demands, new properties and new projects send one email a day. Confir

- **BR-PD-1576** — Control Panel operators sign in with email and password and share no sign-in with the customer app. _(1. Two separate identities)_

- **BR-PD-1578** — There is no self-registration for operators; a super admin or admin creates the account. _(2.1 Credentials)_
- **BR-PD-1579** — New and reset operator accounts receive a one-time password by email. _(2.1 First sign-in)_

- **BR-PD-1581** — Password rule: at least 6 characters with one uppercase letter, one number and one special character; the form lists what is missing. _(2.1 Password rules)_
- **BR-PD-1582** — When two-factor is on for the environment, a 6-digit code is emailed after the password; it lasts 5 minutes and works once. _(2.1 Two-factor code)_

- **BR-PD-1584** — 5 wrong codes void the code. _(2.1 Code limits)_

- **BR-PD-1586** — At most 5 codes are issued per person in 15 minutes. _(2.1 Code limits)_
- **BR-PD-1587** — If code delivery fails, sign-in fails with a "try again" message; the system never lets someone in because email failed. _(2.1 Code delivery failure)_
- **BR-PD-1588** — 5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes; it unlocks by itself and a correct sign-in resets the count. _(2.1 Password lockout)_

- **BR-PD-1592** — The session idle limit is 24 hours in every environment. _(6. Feature Switches)_

- **BR-PD-1595** — Reusing an old session token signs the person out everywhere and is logged. _(2.1 Stolen-session protection)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Analytics (Google Analytics tile) is a placeholder; permission exists, no screen.
- Content Management and Site Down permissions reserved for a later phase; no screen.
- No per-item read state on the bell; it uses a "last seen" time.
- Agent deletion is final; there is no admin undelete for agents. Deleted HVL rules cannot be restored.
- Two-factor cannot be switched from the panel; controlled from the AWS console by ops.
- Inferred, not verified: exact tabs/buttons on detail pages; role editor layout; Formats screen entry points; moderation notification delivery; which environments set enforce-agent-subscription on; exact production newsletter/digest recipients; Insights part lists (code manifest is source of truth); whether web signals and sign-up attribution are on in production (default off); final contact-request notification copy; undated changes after 2026-11-03 may be missing.
- Section 5.3 admin-team notifications: specified 2026-11-03, build status and recipients still to be confirmed.

- Product question 2: should an Admin see Technical Insights by default (today yes)?
- Product question 3: should assign-lead use "unlock" instead of "manage rules" (today someone who can release may not be able to assign)?
- Product question 4: should email-domain rules and staff management share one permission (today both need adminusers.manage)?
- Product question 5: should deleted HVL rules be restorable (today no)?
- Product question 6: should panel-posted demands respect agent subscription by default (today off unless an environment sets it)?
- Product question 7: who receives admin-team emails in 5.3 (shared inbox, all active super admins/admins, or configurable list), and should bell alerts follow role permissions?
- Product question 8: how to handle high-volume bell alerts (contact viewed, images requested, contact requested, phone viewed).
- Product question 9 is cut off mid-sentence in the source ("Confir…"); the daily-summary send time question is incomplete.
- Ambiguity: 6 shows Messaging hold "Push only" for UAT, while 5.2 says the hold applies on DEV and SIT only.
- Ambiguity: section 2.2 says a custom role can be changed by "Admin or super admin, within limits" but 2.3 says built-in roles are read-only to non-super admins; custom-role editing limits beyond "no self-escalation" are not specified.
- Conflict: this doc (4.19) limits Recent Activity to marketing enquiries and listing leads, while Functional Flows 36 says "View all" also lists admin team notifications.
- Conflict: this doc (5.3) states build status of admin-team notifications is "to be confirmed", while Functional Flows 38 says nothing is in the code yet (specification only).
- Conflict: Agent subscribed email body wording differs between this doc (5.3) and Functional Flows 38; pending sign-up subject differs between this doc/Flow 38 ("[User type]") and the persona doc ("[User type], [Mobile number]").

##### Admin Control Panel — End-to-End Functional Flows

> **Audience:** operations, customer success, QA and product. **Status date:** 2026-11-05. **Companion documents:** [01 — Product Documentation](./01-product-documentation.md) (access model, permissions, navigation, features) · [Operator persona flow](../personas/09-control-panel-operator.md) **Reading guide:** each flow names the **actor**, what must be true first, the **steps** (with validations and success and failure outcomes), the **side effects** (notifications and audit), and **edge cases**. Permission names refer to the matrix in the product documentation.
